operational.activation: Reaction — when another creature you can perceive within range and line of effect begins casting a spell, after its casting costs and cadence are committed but before its effect resolves
operational.targets: One pending spell cast by the triggering creature. The spell needs an actual recorded rank; the Director may know that rank without revealing it to you.
operational.resolution: make a spellcasting-ability check using the actual ability for the class through which you cast Counterspell, adding PB once, against DC 10 + twice the triggering spell's actual rank (rank 0 contributes 0). Use CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md's fixed-DC task degrees and natural shifts: at least DC+10 Critical Success, at least DC Success, at most DC-10 Critical Failure, otherwise Failure; natural 20 improves one degree and natural 1 worsens one. Collapse both upper degrees to success and both lower degrees to failure; invent no additional critical effect. This is not a spell attack or saving throw.
operational.effect: Success negates the selected pending spell after its costs were committed; failure lets it continue. Every interruptible cast first commits its RP/material/other costs, components, concentration transition, Dissonance/Refrain and exact beginning/casting hooks once, then opens the interruption window. A surviving cast later resolves its effect and outcome-dependent hooks. Negation gives no refund, no successful-effect trigger and no restoration of old concentration. Counterspell is itself a spell and can be countered. Resolve nested counters last-in, first-out; if a counter is negated, the earlier pending spell resumes without paying or casting again. Resuming a parent never rewrites the later nested cast's Refrain/Dissonance history.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic success against lower ranks and no generic upcast.
operational.limitations: One attempt per creature against a particular pending cast, shared across ordinary, Wizard, Mage and other same-named Counterspell sources. An exact source that expressly grants an additional Counterspell attempt against the same pending cast overrides this default; merely granting another Reaction does not. After a failed attempt another eligible creature may react; once negated, the spell supplies no further interruption trigger. All reactions need their own legal remaining resource, components, range and current source permissions. Attempting does not reveal spell identity/rank; never treat an unassigned rank as 0 or estimate it from RP. Ready opens its cast-interruption window at preparation, not release. Countering is not whole-Action/turn hard denial and does not spend that ledger. Ordinary Counterspell requires ordinary repertoire/class access and rank-3 cost; Wizard/Mage same-named class cards keep their own separate acquisition, printed costs, ranks, recharge and text. Apply SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md for actual class access and repertoire, costs before resolution, components, concentration, Dissonance/Refrain and exact source cadence. No automatic scaling or generic upcast.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: both Abjuration/Universal rank-3 placements, Reaction, 60 feet, V/S/F and instantaneous interruption. NEW: actual casting ability+PB against DC 10+2*rank, one attempt per pending cast, hidden-rank handling and nested timing. REVIEWED SOURCE CORRECTION: the earlier binary-check proposal is superseded by the existing Core fixed-DC task rule, with natural shifts and collapsed success/failure outcomes. Exact source permission may override the shared attempt limit; another Reaction alone cannot.

# Spell integration rules — provisional v0.1

Use this document with the [shared class rules](CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md), the class's own engine and the [spell packet](SPELL_PLAYTEST_STARTER.md). This is a staged development layer, not an approved-book replacement or a live companion update.

## What owns each decision

| Decision | Source used for this packet |
|---|---|
| Spell identity, every school placement and per-class rank/access | Preserved `src/data/spells.js`; do not collapse different class ranks into one global rank. |
| Common RP prices and additional spell evidence | Core Systems Known Descent V2. Its spell blocks are retained with the catalog summaries. |
| Class identity, engine, spellbook/preparation and cadence exceptions | The current class playtest packet. |
| Generic Dissonance/Refrain, action limits and core conditions | Shared class playtest rules; source Core conditions remain unchanged. |
| Missing targeting, exact endpoints, concentration ambiguities and exploit limits | Explicitly provisional decisions on each spell card. |

The approved Core V2 source has 936 spell blocks. The companion catalog has 848 unique IDs with 936 school placements, but leaves four metadata fields unspecified. These are different views of the source, not evidence that all casting details were absent. Core's generic “Automatic or opposed as described” does not supply a concrete save or targeting rule.

Eleven possible renamed entries remain comparative evidence in the register. Harmonic Bulwark's catalog summary says 5 temporary HP per RP while the possible historical Mana Shield entry says 2; its [individual transformation and buffer review](TRANSFORMATION_SPELL_PLAYTEST.md) now supplies the operational decision. Both source variants remain preserved. Other unresolved aliases stay pending their own review; matching names never silently merge effects.

Resonance Kindle now has [exact manuscript approval](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_CONJURATION_CANTRIP_EXACT_REVIEW.md): Action/Self/V/S, recover 1 RP only when this spell reaches resolution. Its one character-wide use is spent at legal cast start and refreshes only on a beneficial completed long rest. The comparative Mana Kindle block remains separately preserved; its broader wording does not trigger recovery from other cantrips and its historical range grants no remote recipient. The [Conjuration cantrip status](CONJURATION_CANTRIP_REVIEW_STATUS.json) records this bounded decision and the other eleven approved cards.

## Select a spell

1. Choose the class through which you are learning/casting it. Check that class's school access and minimum **class** level on the card.
2. Use that class's spell rank and Core V2 cost. A different eligible class may receive the same spell at a different rank and level.
3. Record it in your allowed known, prepared or spellbook choices. An eligible catalog entry is not an automatic grant. Wizard and Druid keep their explicit preparation systems; fallback counts apply only where the class has no more specific rule.

## Falling bridge — new provisional procedure

This is a newly authored table procedure agreed with the GPT notebook, **not recovered V6/Core V2 canon**. Focused searches of the current rulebook extract, Core V2 and mechanics/manual text found spell summaries but no operational falling clock or impact formula. Before promotion to canon, inspect the approved V6 environment/travel/hazard sections and archived environment tables. Preserve any older rule found and compare it explicitly.

When a creature loses support with no movement mode or effect keeping it aloft, it enters **Falling** immediately. Falling means unsupported; it grants no hovering, airborne walking or lateral movement. Track total distance descended during this fall and cumulative distance during its current uncontrolled portion, both initially zero.

**Timing:** If a fall begins during a regular initiative turn, set a fixed Fall Marker at the **end of that initiative slot in the following round**. Resolve the first Falling Step there, then one at the same marker each round. Reactions and extra turns use the enclosing regular initiative slot; an event between slots uses the most recently completed slot. Extra turns, extra Actions and initiative changes neither move nor multiply the marker. This gives every participant one normal turn opportunity before the first descent; inability to act still matters and no free rescue action is granted. A caster still needs legal targets within range when spending their Action.

Outside initiative, when timing matters, establish an order before descent and use a virtual slot immediately before its first regular slot as the initiating slot. The first step occurs when that virtual slot next recurs, after everyone has had one normal turn opportunity. When no rescue or other timing decision is possible, the Director can resolve the same descent and impact calculation directly. This is an explicit timing abstraction, not a model of physical acceleration.

If a fall begins after initiative has been established but before any regular initiative slot has yet completed, treat the virtual pre-round slot as the most recently completed slot for Fall Marker purposes.

**Ordinary descent:** At each step descend up to **300 feet**, stopping on a supporting surface. Add the distance to both trackers. On landing while uncontrolled, take **min(10, floor(uncontrolled distance / 20))d6 bludgeoning damage**. The uncontrolled distance includes earlier steps; never use only the final step's remainder.

**Feather Fall:** The spell retains its **Action** casting time and reduces descent to at most **60 feet per step**. When it takes effect, set uncontrolled distance to zero: the magic dissipates prior uncontrolled momentum in this abstraction. Keep total fall distance. If landing while it remains active, damage is **min(3, floor(total fall distance / 20))d6 bludgeoning**. This explicitly limits impact exposure without guaranteeing a harmless landing. When the spell ends aloft, reset uncontrolled distance to zero, then accumulate ordinary descent from that point at the existing marker; expiry grants no immediate extra step. Its one-minute maximum ends immediately before the caster's regular turn ten rounds after casting. If expiry and a step coincide, resolve expiry first. Earlier landing or cessation of Falling ends the spell on that target as printed.

Apply damage defenses only when their actual wording covers that damage. After damage, Falling ends; a creature suffering any positive falling damage lands **Prone** unless an explicit feature prevents it. Less than 20 relevant feet produces zero damage. Forced movement that removes support starts a fall but adds no separate fall damage. Regaining genuine support, secure support from a hold, or flight ends Falling without resolving an uncompleted impact; teleporting safely onto support likewise ends it. A later loss of support begins a new fall with new trackers and marker. Completed impact and damage cannot be undone by later casting.

**Resonance Influence:** compute ordinary legal spell price first, including mandatory extras, Dissonance, eligible source reductions/waivers and each feature's own minimum. ## Which rule applies

The domain authority is [Core Systems Known Descent V2](../../../../books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx). The approved [Player Rulebook V6](../../../../books/player/Decennium_Descent_Player_Rulebook_v6.docx) supplies compatible rules that Core does not replace. This overlay states the selected interpretation or newly authored rule wherever those sources leave a gap. An explicit exception on an operative, reviewed class/spell/item card applies only within its printed scope; a historical alternate or a same-named feature is not an extra grant. This candidate does not promote an entire historical branch.

| Question | Active rule and provenance | Inactive alternate |
|---|---|---|
| Attacks | Core V2: meet AC; natural 1 misses; natural 20 hits and doubles damage dice. | Applying the general Gameplay four-degree roll to attacks. |
| Task checks | Explicitly adopted Gameplay four degrees and natural shifts. | Assuming every critical result creates an unprinted effect. |
| Ordinary saves | Binary meet-DC test; printed failure margins remain literal. Natural 1/20 do not generically shift saves in this candidate. This separation is an integration choice. | Automatic critical saves or natural-result shifts inferred from the task rule. |
| Death-save timing | Core and V6: start of turn; regular-turn-only timing is a provisional guard. | Gameplay end-of-turn saves. |
| Wounds | Core trigger/save, Constitution-save and Hit-Dice-recovery penalties, and three-Wound Critical state. | Gameplay automatic Wound triggers, Hit Dice healing penalty, half Speed and Strain lock. |
| Named Wounded condition | Core paragraph 782 expressly describes the same Wound count, Constitution penalty, Hit Dice recovery and three-Wound Critical state. Apply those records once. | V6 Appendix A paragraphs 9971–9974 give a conflicting temporary condition cleared by magic/rest with Constitution-save disadvantage; Core replaces it here. |
| Stable, instant death, knockout and temporary HP | Compatible recovered V6 rules. | Treating these recovered rules as newly invented. |
| Ordinary Wound treatment | Explicit Gameplay-derived integration below. | Claiming it is original Core wording or ordinary HP healing. |
| Injury table and unresolved thresholds | New provisional choices below, with their search limits stated. | Dropping Core's failure-by-5 consequence because its table was not located. |

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Rolls
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Rolls

Choose the roll type before rolling. Use the actual ability modifier, including negative values, and normal proficiency only when applicable. Existing advantage/disadvantage chooses the higher/lower of two d20s; multiple sources do not stack, and any advantage plus disadvantage cancels. Add other legal modifiers once. Fractions round down unless a rule specifies otherwise. One tile is 5 feet. Class L, S and effect M retain their definitions in the shared class rules.

**Attack:** roll d20 plus the appropriate attack modifier against AC. Meeting AC hits. Natural 1 always misses; natural 20 always hits and critically doubles damage dice, not flat modifiers. Beating AC by 10 is not a critical hit. An explicit broader critical range does not stack with another; use the broadest eligible range. In this overlay, a natural result below 20 in that range must still meet AC unless the feature expressly says it always hits.

**Task, skill or tool check against a fixed DC:** total at least DC+10 is Critical Success; at least DC is Success; at most DC-10 is Critical Failure; other totals below DC are Failure. Natural 20 then improves one degree and natural 1 worsens one, bounded at either end. A task printing only success/failure collapses the two upper degrees to success and two lower degrees to failure; no extra consequence is invented. A natural 20 can still fail an otherwise impossible check, and a natural 1 with sufficient modifiers can still succeed.

**Saving throw:** total at least DC succeeds; otherwise it fails. Natural 1 and 20 have no generic special outcome. A printed failure by 5 or 10 compares the final total with the DC; it does not add an unprinted critical-save system. Death saves are the specific exception below.

**Opposed check, new provisional tie rule:** compare final totals. Higher wins; an exact tie leaves the existing state unchanged, so the initiating creature fails to change it. Do not turn task natural shifts into hidden numeric modifiers. A maneuver explicitly printing degree outcomes must specify how those apply.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Resolve a damage event
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Resolve a damage event

Resolve each genuinely separate hit or damage event once. Do not split one packet to multiply Wound saves or combine separate hits merely to cross a threshold. Feature-specific prevention that acts before damage or before reaching zero resolves at its printed timing first.

1. Resolve attack/save, damage and applicable defenses. The remaining nonnegative amount is **resolved damage**.
2. Record HP, Wounds and zero-HP state before the event. Remove temporary HP first. **Post-temp damage = resolved damage minus temporary HP absorbed.** Keep this amount even when it exceeds current HP; floor the resulting current HP at zero.
3. Check V6 Instant Death. If post-temp damage minus HP before the hit is at least maximum HP, the creature dies. For a creature already at zero, this is post-temp damage at least maximum HP. Stop: there is no Wound save, death-save failure or successful knockout from that event.
4. Otherwise, a living creature makes one Wound save if it dropped from positive HP to zero, if **2 × post-temp damage is at least maximum HP**, or if the effect actually inflicts Maiming. Overlapping triggers still cause only one save. The post-temp threshold and one-save rule are new provisional interpretations. Maiming is an independent trigger even when temporary HP absorbs all ordinary damage; immunity to Maiming itself still applies.
5. Make a Constitution save against **max(10, floor(post-temp damage / 2))**. Use pre-event Wounds for the -1-per-Wound penalty. Maiming with zero post-temp damage uses DC 10. A Wound gained now cannot penalize the roll that created it.
6. A success adds no Wound. A failure that began with zero, one or two Wounds adds exactly one; failure by 5 or more also gives that Wound one Injury. A failure that began with three Wounds kills the creature instead: no fourth Wound and no Injury roll. Stop processing later living-target consequences if dead.
7. If the creature was already at zero before this event and post-temp damage is positive, end Stable. A creature using death saves adds one failure, or two for a critical hit; three failures kill it. An ordinary creature that does not use death saves dies instead, without starting death counters. A hit from positive HP to zero does not also cause a same-packet death failure.
8. If this event newly reduces positive HP to zero, a valid melee knockout makes the surviving creature Stable. Otherwise a character/significant NPC using death saves begins dying; an ordinary monster dies. A previously Stable creature whose temporary HP absorbed all damage remains Stable unless an independent Maiming result killed it. The Director identifies significant NPCs consistently. Knockout cannot override Instant Death or a fatal Wound save.

Core's Maiming and Wound trigger rules remain subject to an actual feature's eligibility. The reference helper receives already legal events; it does not grant every attack Maiming or a damage-prevention exception.

currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Encounter and action resources

Establish terrain, light, hazards, objectives, exits and cargo; determine awareness; roll `d20 + DEX modifier + legal bonuses`. Highest first. Players choose player/player ties; the Director resolves ties involving NPCs. Keep the resulting ordered slots for the encounter. A round represents approximately six seconds. A **regular turn** is a creature's normal initiative slot even if it cannot act. An extra turn is distinct.

A turn normally permits movement, one Action, a Bonus Action when an actual rule grants a use, and one ordinary free object interaction. A second ordinary interaction or an Action-time object activation uses an Action. Brief communication is not an extra Action. Conditions and specific features may restrict these permissions.

The shared limit is one **extra full Action per creature per numbered round**. Such an Action cannot grant another extra Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. This cap is independent of Reaction timing. Extra turns do not by themselves refresh Reactions, recharge, periodic ticks, recovery ticks or the regular-turn allowances defined here.

**Reaction interpretation.** Begin an encounter with one available Reaction unless surprised or otherwise prohibited. Refresh at each regular own-turn start; never at the numbered round boundary or an extra turn. A late-initiative creature can therefore react before its first turn, refresh, and react again in the same numbered round. A legal trigger, available resource and all feature prerequisites are still required.

**Explicit additional Reactions.** A reviewed card can grant a separate limited use without refreshing the ordinary resource. Warrior Mind Shock supplies its stated once-per-duration non-attack Reaction; spending one resource does not consume/reset the other. Surprise, Incapacitated and Focused still restrict both. It grants no Counterspell knowledge or waived costs. Extra turns refresh neither. Per-dose reapplication/stacking and other specific grants remain part of the class semantic pass.

**Surprise — V6 plus NEW Bonus Action clarification.** On a surprised creature's first regular turn it cannot voluntarily move or take an Action or Bonus Action. It cannot react until that turn ends. Its slot, durations, passive effects, concentration, periodic effects and recharge still occur. Surprise alone is not Incapacitated or Unconscious. Brief communication and an otherwise legal simple free interaction remain possible.

**Entry — NEW.** Standard end-round reinforcements roll/receive initiative and first act next round. An explicit midround entrant acts this round only if its complete ordered slot is still upcoming; entry during that exact slot counts as already passed. It has its initial Reaction unless prohibited. A summon-specific timing rule overrides this generic entry procedure.

After the final slot, resolve Core's end-round hazards, reinforcements, morale, objectives and boss phases. Conclude the scene with surrender, capture, pursuit, harvesting access and noise consequences under their own rules; winning initiative does not resolve those automatically.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Time and event ordering — NEW
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Time and event ordering — NEW

For a duration created in initiative, record the relevant original regular start/end marker. Existing effects keep that **virtual marker**, repeating every six seconds if the creature leaves or changes initiative. Reordering, rerolling, extra turns, death/removal or leaving/reentering initiative never restart an existing duration. New effects use the current schedule. Source death still ends concentration, a source-dependent aura/tether or an effect explicitly ending on death.

- A bare hostile target-bound **N rounds** ends at the Nth future regular target-end marker. An in-progress target turn's current end does not count.
- A bare self/source buff, ally-targeted buff or source-controlled aura **N rounds** ends at the Nth future source-start marker. Explicit target-turn, pulse or absolute timing overrides this default. Activation during source turn 1 for three rounds ends at source turn 4's start.
- **Next turn** means the next future regular turn of the named creature, not the current turn's still-upcoming end. An unqualified next turn refers to source/user under the existing shared rule. Explicit “this turn” can include the current turn.
- An outside-initiative bare N-round effect instead gets an absolute application-time + N×6 seconds deadline. Entering initiative preserves that deadline.
- Explicit periodic profiles retain their registered clocks and tick counts. Never create a second timer merely because a generic duration rule also exists.

The [exact GPT review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_COMBAT_EXACT_FINDINGS.md) confirms ally-buff source clocks and excluding the current turn for explicit next-turn endpoints. The helper excludes a specific current-end marker only if that marker would otherwise be selected: application during a turn at time1 with end3 excludes3 and selects9; application at/after3 also selects9, without erroneously skipping again to15.

At a regular turn's **start**, resolve in this order:

1. Expire start-ending effects and apply immediate state changes from those expirations.
2. Refresh Reaction; tick regular-start recharge/non-action clocks.
3. Resolve already-due absolute state recovery if now legal, including a previously blocked Stable recovery deadline.
4. If still alive, dying and at 0 HP with death saves, make that turn's death save.
5. Resolve other start effects and periodic events in application order.
6. Begin voluntary turn decisions.

At **end**, resolve triggered effects, due damage, saves and maintenance before end-ending effects expire; then the slot finishes. No extra turn creates another regular marker. The caller must not reuse a resolved marker.

For simultaneous effects, earlier application timestamp precedes later. For simultaneous components of one source, its printed internal order controls; otherwise use stable application sequence, with source/mechanical ID as a final tie-break. Record that sequence when creating the effects. Beneficial/harmful labels do not change priority. Periodic family arbitration happens once per family/marker before its damage, retaining the family registry's consumed loser ticks.

Examples: dying at 0 rolls its death save before ordinary start-turn healing; a fatal death save is not undone by ordinary healing. Stable at 0 skips the save, then start-turn damage can break Stable. A natural 20 can restore 1 HP before a due Bleed drops it to 0 as a new drop event. If Decay expires while a Stable recovery deadline is already due, the old deadline resolves once without rerolling recovery time.

currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Standard Actions

| Action | Procedure |
|---|---|
| Attack | Make the attacks legally granted by class and weapon. Replacing one attack does not replace the entire Action unless specified. |
| Cast | Use an Action-time spell or Resonance technique; all known/prepared, cost, component and target requirements apply. |
| Dash | Add one current Speed to each mode's turn cap; see movement ledger. Speed 0 grants none. A second legally paid Dash adds another Speed. |
| Disengage | Voluntary movement does not provoke opportunity attacks for the rest of that turn. |
| Dodge | Until next regular start, attacks from attackers you can see have disadvantage; your DEX saves have advantage. Benefit fails while Incapacitated or Speed 0. |
| Guard | +2 AC against the first attack against you before next regular start; consumed on that attack hit or miss. Guard state and Interpose permission remain until expiry even after the +2 is spent. |
| Aim | Action; no prior voluntary movement this turn, and no subsequent voluntary movement that turn. +2 to one ranged/spell attack before turn end. Forced movement does not cancel it. It grants no attack; a legal Bonus Action/extra Action/express attack must supply one. |
| Help | Advantage on a relevant ally check before next regular start, or assist an attack against a foe within 5 ft: the helped ally's first attack before that deadline has advantage. Assistance must be physically possible. |
| Hide / Search | Use the observer-specific procedures below. |
| Ready | Prepare an Action or movement; release uses Reaction as detailed below. |
| Use Object | Pay for the second ordinary interaction or an object's required Action activation. No extra hands/capacity are granted. |
| Improvise | Director declares ability, applicable proficiency, DC/opposed method and intended consequence before rolling. Success does not create unannounced conditions/actions. |

**Brace — NEW.** Action, choose one mode until next regular start. **Intercept:** choose a breach/doorway edge or current melee reach; when a hostile creature charges/leaps/breaches into it and enters legal reach, spend Reaction for one legal melee weapon attack after entry and before later movement/actions. **Hold Ground:** spend Reaction on the first applicable discrete push/pull/shove/knockback to reduce displacement 5 ft, minimum 0. It does not reduce damage, prevent independent Prone, stop gravity/fall steps, currents, conveyors, collapsing ground or teleportation, or grant support/hover. One Brace supplies one opportunity, not an extra Reaction.

**Rally — NEW.** Action; choose one ally within 30 ft able to perceive the rally and one active source-qualified Frightened record. CHA check at that record's source DC, otherwise 10; Success/Critical Success ends only that record. A later reviewed morale rule can supply a separate specific interaction. No automatic temporary HP, loyalty, belief or advantage.

**Withdraw.** Action; separate half-current-Speed movement budget, normal terrain costs, no opportunity attacks from that movement and +2 AC only while that movement resolves. Speed 0 grants none. Moving zero grants no lingering +2. Ordinary movement before/after remains separate. The separate budget is NEW interpretation of Core 480.

**Secure Cargo.** Core 482 preserves the wording “up to one Extraction Load class.” The subsequently reviewed [body and carrying guide](BODY_EQUIPMENT_PLAYTEST.md) supplies the provisional interpretation: spend an Action on one legal attach, lift, transfer or protective operation involving one actual cargo unit or physically constituted bundle with an assigned Extraction Class. Load measures burden; Extraction Class measures danger and logistics. Apply actual capacity, custody, hands, harnesses, checks and durability. The Action grants no extra capacity, equipment, automatic success, invulnerability or reduction in Extraction Class. Full equipment and extraction catalogs remain open.

currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Ready

Spend an Action to declare a perceivable trigger and one legal Action-time action or movement. It expires next regular own-turn start. **NEW:** only one pending Ready per creature; replacing it loses the prior setup and any paid held-spell costs. No Bonus Action/Reaction ability, long ritual or multi-minute activity can be prepared by generic Ready.

The trigger happens first, then the readied response immediately follows before later events, unless a specific effect explicitly interrupts. On release spend the normal Reaction and recheck target, range, sight/perception, line of effect, ammunition and other prerequisites. An invalid or declined occurrence spends no release resource; the Ready can wait for another valid occurrence before expiry. This does not undo setup costs. Once released, it is consumed.

For ordinary nonspell actions, feature/ammunition costs are paid on release unless text charges setup. A readied **Attack Action** gets its legally available ordinary attack count; a feature limited to your own turn does not thereby work off-turn. Core Overwatch is explicitly one ranged attack, not that full Attack Action and not Soldier's distinct engine.

A readied spell is actually **cast at preparation**: choose spell/mode, verify legality, pay RP/material/other costs, provide components, resolve Dissonance/Refrain and cast-trigger effects once. Counterspell/cast-interruption opportunity occurs then, not again at release. Every held spell requires concentration, even ordinarily non-concentration spells; incompatible prior concentration ends. Lost concentration loses the held spell and costs. NEW: select the legal target/area point at release and recheck legality without repaying. At release the hold continues as ordinary spell concentration if required, otherwise ends after resolution. Expired/replaced/countered held spells do not refund paid costs.

Ready movement grants a separate current-Speed budget on release, pays terrain costs and can provoke ordinary opportunity attacks. It grants no extra Action, Bonus Action or interaction.

Focused stance's Reaction restriction also blocks an ordinary Ready release; Ready does not create a Counterspell exception. Holding a spell does not waive any current Reaction prohibition.

**Spell-effect duration begins at release.** Its normal duration is anchored when the effect manifests, while Ready expiry and held concentration already run from preparation. A source explicitly tying a particular consequence to casting/preparation retains that consequence's stated clock. No casting cost, Refrain, Dissonance or cast trigger occurs a second time merely from release.

currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Movement and geometry

Track **spent movement cost**, not distance, for ordinary turn movement. Mode cap = `(1 + number of legal Dash actions this turn) × current Speed for that mode`; remaining = max(0, cap − spent cost). Switching modes never refunds cost. Recalculate cap on Speed changes, preserving spent cost. Stand from Prone costs floor(half current Speed) and requires nonzero Speed and enough budget. Dropping Prone costs no movement.

For each foot traveled, normal/difficult/severe terrain costs 1/2/3; use strongest terrain only. Add +1 for crawling and +1 for squeezing. Crawl in difficult =3:1; crawl+squeeze in difficult =4:1. A nonhostile occupied space counts as difficult terrain. Enter a hostile creature's space only with ≥two-size difference or an express feature; never willingly end in an occupied space. Squeeze through a space one size smaller, with own attack/DEX-save disadvantage and attacks-against advantage.

Walk10 through difficult spends20; switch to Fly30 leaves10. Stand with Speed30 spends15; switching to Fly30 leaves15. Two legal Dashes at Speed30 give cap90; prior expenditure still counts. Interpose/Press grant5 budget: they cannot enter a difficult 5-ft tile costing10. Their separate budgets never refill ordinary movement. Ready movement uses Speed at release; Withdraw uses half current Speed. All voluntary movement requires nonzero relevant Speed.

Forced movement does not use these ledgers or provoke ordinary opportunity attacks, cannot place creatures in solid matter, and stops at obstacles. Teleport does not traverse intervening terrain or spend Speed unless printed; it requires a legal destination. Speed0 alone does not block forced movement or teleport. Flight with Prone/Speed0/lost support causes Falling unless Hover or an explicit magical support exception applies; use the existing fixed Fall Marker procedure. Reaching support ends Falling.

NEW grid metric: each orthogonal or diagonal neighboring tile is 5 ft; use the same metric for ordinary ranges/areas. No diagonal cut through a corner when both adjacent orthogonal sides are completely blocked. Exact templates, 3D geometry, mounts, chases, jumping, climbing/swimming procedures and currents need further source review.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Cover, sight, Hide and Search
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Cover, sight, Hide and Search

Keep **visibility**, **known location**, and **line of effect** separate. Seeing through a barrier does not itself permit attacking through it. Best cover only: half +2 AC/DEX saves; three-quarters +5; total prevents direct targeting through that obstruction. Never add +2 and +5. For areas, evaluate line/cover from the area's origin to each target; total cover there excludes a creature unless the effect explicitly travels around/through the obstruction. The origin point itself must be legally targetable.

Within normal ranged range, no range penalty; beyond normal through long, disadvantage; beyond long, illegal. Ranged attacks also have disadvantage when within5ft of a non-Incapacitated hostile that can see the attacker, even if the attacker cannot see that hostile. All advantage/disadvantage follows the single cancellation rule.

NEW **Hide**: permitted only against observers unable to see you clearly or where a feature permits. Roll DEX Stealth once, record natural die and total. Against each observer's passive DC `10 + WIS Perception modifier including applicable proficiency`, use the Core four-degree task system. Meet DC succeeds before natural1/20 degree adjustment; Success/Critical Success establishes Hidden for that observer. No unsourced passive ±5 adjustment for advantage/disadvantage. Actual Search rolls use their normal modifiers.

Hidden means that observer cannot see you and does not know your location. Clear sight or learning your position ends Hidden for that observer. Moving between hiding places can retain Hidden only if no clear sight/revealing event occurs. A failed Hide cannot simply be rerolled unchanged; a materially new hiding position, concealment, distraction, sight-breaking event or express reroll feature is required. Hidden is not a generic immunity or a free stealth roll for every move.

**Search** Action: WIS Perception for sensory detection; INT Investigation for appropriate traces/deduction; Core Arcana/Engineering where relevant. Directly locating a Hidden creature defaults to Perception against its recorded final Stealth total as a static DC, using task degrees/natural shifts. Success reveals location only to the searcher and ends Hidden for that observer, without automatically granting sight. Communicate normally to inform others. Search can be repeated on later turns by paying the Action.

Attacks against unseen targets have disadvantage; unseen attackers have advantage, subject to the **Core Invisible exception**: once its position is known, Invisible's own attack modifiers end for that observer and cannot immediately return solely because it remains Invisible. Independent darkness, smoke, blindness or hiding can still supply modifiers.

Resolve an attack using pre-attack information; afterward reveal location to observers able to perceive its evidence. If an unseen target's location is unknown, do not directly choose it for a creature-target effect. A weapon/projectile can instead attack a suspected space: wrong space automatically misses; correct space uses unseen rules. A “creature you can see” requirement is never met by position knowledge alone. Area effects can target legal points under their own rules.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Records, clocks and precedence
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Records, clocks and precedence

Each application records its identity, exact source, owner character, target, selected mode/components, application order, recorded source DC, deadline/marker, concentration or attachment relationship, remaining uses, and applicable immunity/suppression. Display names never create conditions or prerequisites. An owner's mark cannot satisfy another owner's class hook. A corpse marker, map point, archived spell, intrinsic Oracle Curse and hard-denial history are distinct state types.

Explicit operative effect text controls over a less-specific summary duration field. Use preserved regular-turn markers for **next** turn and bare N-round durations as in the combat guide; an in-progress current turn is not the next turn. Unqualified next turn refers to the source; explicit its/target refers to the target. Bare hostile N rounds, including hostile marks, use N future target regular ends. Beneficial/self N rounds use source regular starts. Preserve virtual markers through initiative changes and absence. Out of initiative bare N rounds use application+6N seconds, retaining that deadline on entering initiative. Explicit source/concentration endings still apply.

**NEW current-turn bridge:** “end of that turn” or the supplied bare “end turn” effects end at the end of the actual turn containing the application event, including another creature's or an extra turn. With no current turn, use application+6 seconds. An application during end-turn resolution expires at that same end after resolving, rather than acquiring a fabricated next turn. This applies to Resonant Seed, Winter's Embrace, Frost Totem and Glue. It does not override an explicit next-turn endpoint.

The reference represents an expiry as an ordered `(seconds, phase)` marker, preserving exact rational seconds from the combat clock. Every turn-end deadline uses expiry phase 20: current actual turn, source/target next regular end, Nth future target regular end, and Balanced Elements' following target end. End-trigger application/resolution occurs at phase 10 and the next event slot at phase 30. The effect therefore remains during final end events and expires afterward at that same second. Turn-start and absolute elapsed deadlines use phase 0. Callers must choose an explicit typed deadline; bare numeric expiries are rejected. No fractional-second workaround or duplicate turn is created.

Repeat saves, ordinary duration expiry and previously reviewed periodic/recharge clocks use regular turns unless an explicit exception applies. This is **not** a global rule changing every “each turn” damage trigger. Zone entry/start application checks, repeat ending saves and once-per-numbered-round caps are distinct events. Follow each source's actual trigger and cap; concentration alone grants no recurring application save.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Marks and one-use components
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Marks and one-use components

Marks retain owner, target type/cap, source clock, independent rider entitlements and eligibility tags. They are not automatically Core Marked or mutually interchangeable. Trigger wording matters: next attack spends on the qualifying attack roll; next hit spends on a qualifying hit even if damage becomes0; when damaged requires a positive resolved-damage packet after defenses but before temporaryHP. Only the component named by a consumption event ends, unless the source says the whole mark ends.

**Reviewed healing-conference clarification:** numeric actualDamageDealt is tempHP absorbed plus actual normalHP lost to the packet, excluding overkill and later recovery/state assignments. A positive packet against an HP1 floor can have numeric0: Divine Judgment still reflects its minimum1 and consumes that actual turn's entitlement. A fully prevented resolved0 packet does neither. The [healing guide](HEALING_DEATH_PLAYTEST.md) defines the complete distinction; this clarification adds2 checks to the previously reviewed148-case control scope.

Guiding Star's reference API begins the legal qualifying attack **before** rolling: consume the available+2 entitlement and return the bonus plus a unique attack token. After the roll, resolve that token once with the hit outcome to receive any remainingS radiant rider. A miss leaves that hit rider for a later ally attack. Duplicate or foreign token resolution is rejected. Suppressed/illegal attack starts spend nothing. If the mark expires or becomes suppressed before resolution, it grants no hit rider; beginning an attack never refunds its spent attack bonus.

| Source | Operational handling |
|---|---|
| Balanced Scales | Actual HP restored to living ally applies mark to source next regular start. First enemy positive damage triggers S+M radiant once, no retaliation recursion. Keep printed at-most-once/marked-ally/round even if healing refreshes. |
| Divine Judgment | First positive damage to another creature on each actual target turn, including extra turns, reflects half actual damage, floor, min1/maxCleric level. No off-turn trigger. Repeat ending WIS saves remain regular-end; concentration/max3 target rounds retained. |
| Carrion Conductor | Corpse-only timed marker. Separate used-corpse history survives expiry, burst or suppression; that corpse cannot be marked again by Carrion Conductor, regardless of owner. It does not ban unrelated corpse mechanics. |
| Drake Mark | One marked target, new replaces old, source next regular end. First subsequent direct polearm hit consumes; triggering leap, DoT or copies do not. AddsS in qualifying hit's damage resolution even if final damage becomes0. |
| Oracle Guiding Bolt | **NEW two entitlements:** first ally-other-than-owner attack gets+2 then spends that opportunity on hit/miss. Next qualifying ally hit before expiry addsS radiant and ends mark. A miss leaves the hit rider, without another+2. New paid application replaces/reset both, never stacks. |
| Oracle Wrathful Brand | Owner's next damaging attack hit adds half unmodified rolled base dice, floor/min1; requires positive pre-bonus resolved attack damage. Separate first ally-positive-damage entitlement attempts1d6 heal and one WIS save; failed save applies printed attack penalty. Heal prevention/full HP does not refund it. Spending riders does not itself end the timed Brand. |
| Oracle Constellation | Owner mark set, printed2 targets/3 mastery; recast replaces previous set. Its+1d6 cap is once/numbered round across set, not per target. |
| Oracle Omen Reader | Triggering -2 attack adjustment consumed once; subsequent star-ash+1 ally attack benefit persists through target-next-end. |
| Paladin Vengeance | Preserve Smite/Brand/Retribution IDs and owner-qualified eligibility. Retribution die consumption does not end its opportunity-attack advantage or remaining mark. |
| Paladin Linked Ward / Chain of Duty | Willing-ally concentration links with separate redirection/teleport triggers, not generic Marked. Ordinary Reaction and printed per-round limits apply. |
| Ranger Track Target | One quarry, new replaces old,1minute; does not reveal through total cover. Predator's Mark upgrades underlying quarry; ending its concentration leaves underlying quarry until its own endpoint. |
| Ranger Pathfinder's Mark | Fixed point,24h; navigation state, not creature condition. |
| Soldier Marked for Death | One target; saves penalty through source-next-start. First qualifying hit against another ally spends its -1 damage rider even if damage0; does not consume the persistent save penalty. No stacking with Intimidating Presence where printed. |
| Tinker Target Scanner | First qualifying ally attack gets+1 and consumes that scanner record on the roll, hit or miss; source-next-start deadline. |
| Wizard Binding Sigil | One target; only owner's Wizard spell attacks gain advantage; source-next-end. No companion/echo/environmental application. |
| Wizard Gravebrand | Source-qualified mark and necrotic periodic effect; the name/Pact does not classify it as an inflicted curse. |

**NEW Divine Judgment simultaneous-target order:** use printed source target order; otherwise declared target/list order fixed before damage, or stable area target application order established before resolving. First recipient taking positive damage supplies reflection magnitude; never sum victims. The turn entitlement is then spent.

Corpses, intrinsic class progression, Monk hard-denial history and Mirrorsage/Wizard archive-retention markers are bookkeeping rather than creature Marked. Existing Crimson Blood Mark, Oracle Mark of the Doomed, Paladin Grief and Warrior Vulnerable identities retain their reviewed rules.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Compulsion, action denial and initiative
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Compulsion, action denial and initiative

Keep Charmed/Frightened, one commanded Action, Reaction denial, Speed0/half and attack restrictions as distinct components. The shared source-character/target/encounter hard-denial guard controls new hard components across feature names. A used allowance blocks only a new hard component; apply an expressly printed soft fallback, otherwise do not invent one. Hard-control immunity and source restrictions still apply.

Oracle Bone Whisper, Ledger's Command, Marquis's Glimpse, Slumber Glimpse and Moment's Pause soft fallback records, and Paladin Decree/Echo of Ages soft fallbacks, carry slowed-foe eligibility only while their actual Speed component is active. Spiral Opens instead has a distinct player-Speed0 component; choosing a repeated action or using NPC Forced Echo does not gain that tag. Passive Stars Revelation Mastery is a HOOK authorizing a later enhanced Guiding Bolt component, not an immediate applied slow. The registry separates application, modifier and reader/bookkeeping references.

Ledger's Command may command one hostile Action under that guard; subsequent qualifying failures use its Reaction+Speed0 fallback. Bone Whisper, Marquis's Glimpse, Slumber Glimpse and Moment's Pause retain their own hard/fallback splits. Slumber's -2 initiative rider affects the next eligible initiative roll/check before encounter end, never an already-established slot. Its attack bonus is independently consumed.

Wizard Mental Binding/Arcane Domination and Paladin Decree of Submission retain only their printed first commanded turn; ongoing Charmed/Reaction/Speed riders cannot command another Action. Mind Prison's first Incapacitated/commanded replacement is separate from later half-Speed/no-Reaction riders. The player retains printed target/route choices and prohibitions on self-harm, beliefs, resource expenditure and permanent allegiance. An NPC Forced Echo from The Spiral Opens spends the hard-denial allowance and has no invented NPC fallback after it is used. Its player branch stays distinct. Royal Decree's target-chosen Prone-or-safe-movement retains Action/target choice and does not spend the whole-Action denial allowance.

Echo of Ages' attack denial uses the shared hard guard; later actual qualifying failed applications use its printed soft fallback. It does not gain a repeat trigger every round from concentration. Reign of Ashes is soft half-Speed/noDash/**no willing teleport benefit**, ending target-next-end. **NEW:** target cannot self-teleport or consent to another's transport; independently legal involuntary hostile displacement can still affect it unless that effect needs willingness. No Root/Restrained or universal planar anchoring is added.

**NEW Moment's Pause delay:** snapshot canonical initiative order excluding temporary delays. One pending delay per target per next numbered round; repeated applications do not stack. At next-round construction process stable application order. Find the first still-participating snapshot creature after the target, skipping removed/dead and ignoring new entrants absent from that snapshot; move target immediately after it. With no surviving later snapshot member leave current position. Chained delays are deterministic in application order; no participant is duplicated/deleted and no virtual duration/falling/recovery marker changes. The next following round resumes canonical order. This is distinct from modifying an initiative roll.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Shared handling
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Shared handling

This overlay governs generic conditions in the combined candidate. A reviewed card overrides a generic clause only where it prints the specific exception. An unreviewed historical summary never grants an extra ability or bypasses a gate. The existing combined source-character/target/encounter hard-denial cap still applies to class/spell/companion applications.

Record each condition source, affected creature, applying DC, magnitude, start, duration and ending method. Same-name nonnumeric penalties apply once; independent sources continue until each ends. A generic cure naming a condition clears its source records unless a reviewed procedure specifies one-record scope. Bleeding Medicine and Burning DEX saves use the specific procedures below. Track Charmed, Frightened, Marked and Grappled relationships separately. Exhaustion, Intoxication, Unity and Wounds use their explicit tracks.

Immunity to a named condition prevents that condition, including an inherited component, but does not silently grant immunity to every parent condition that can cause it. For example, Prone immunity prevents the Prone component of Unconscious, not its other effects. Immunity to an inflicted condition never erases the underlying zero-HP or dead state. Gaining immunity suppresses applicable existing effects while immunity lasts; their clocks continue unless explicitly paused. Removing immunity does not reapply a one-time consequence or restart an old duration.

Advantages and disadvantages never multiply dice: any advantage and any disadvantage cancel to one normal d20 roll, regardless of the number of sources. Automatic failure of a required check/save is resolved without a roll. A condition does not give a save where its source grants none. A critical-if-hit rider never makes a missed attack hit. Automatic failure has no rolled total: use ordinary Failure, not Critical Failure or an invented failure margin, unless the source explicitly supplies one.

Generic Core Bleeding and Burning join family.bleeding and family.ongoing-fire respectively, with source-owner stack groups. At one identical target timing marker, all due generic and custom groups in that family compete: highest expected unmitigated damage, then earliest application. Only the winning group's source-permitted instances deal damage. All due groups consume that tick; losers do not defer or bank it. Different printed markers resolve separately. No record also receives a duplicate generic tick. Core generic timing is end of regular target turn; extra turns do not tick. Outside initiative preserve one periodic step per complete six seconds with no duplicate interval across initiative transitions.

Strain is not globally unique: expedition.strain and warrior.serum-strain are separate source-qualified tracks, both distinct from the six-level Exhaustion condition. See the Strain namespace reference for the current candidate. Oracle one-turn Revelation backlash is also separate from global Exhaustion; its printed penalties and endpoint remain unchanged. Wound Eater feeding failures explicitly use global Exhaustion. Never silently convert similarly named tracks.

See CONDITION_RECOVERY_PLAYTEST.md for finite recovery, cleansing, substance, Intoxication and Unity procedures. These new proposals are labeled separately from recovered source rules. Conditions do not reveal Director secrets or force player beliefs or decisions.

SUPERSESSION — NEW PROVISIONAL INTEGRATION: The unified Bleeding/ongoing-fire family registry supersedes earlier provisional clauses that selected generic records separately, used ending DC as a damage tie-breaker, cleared all generic Bleeding through one Medicine result, or used one Burning save to clear all generic Burning. Original Core quotations and raw review history remain unchanged. See CUSTOM_CONDITION_BINDINGS.md and the recorded GPT_GENERIC_CUSTOM_ALIGNMENT review.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Blinded
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText: ## Blinded **Preserved Core text:** Cannot see; automatically fails sight checks; attacks have disadvantage and attacks against it have advantage. **Effect:** The creature cannot see, automatically fails checks that require sight, has disadvantage on attack rolls, and attack rolls against it have advantage. **Application:** Only an effect that explicitly inflicts Blinded applies it. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's printed duration, save, cure or endpoint. **Stacking:** Multiple Blinded applications do not increase the penalties; track independent durations only when needed to know when all sources have ended. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** A sense that does not require sight may still function. A feature explicitly allowing sight while Blinded overrides only its printed scope. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 matches: cannot see, automatically fails sight-required checks, own attacks have disadvantage, attacks against have advantage. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Full special-senses and vision interaction belongs to the stealth/vision pass. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 731, definition paragraph 732; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json).

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Deafened
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText: ## Deafened **Preserved Core text:** Cannot hear and fails hearing checks; verbal coordination may fail. **Effect:** The creature cannot hear and automatically fails checks that require hearing. It cannot satisfy a rule that specifically requires hearing another creature's command, warning, chant or audible signal. **Application:** Only effects that explicitly inflict Deafened apply it. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's duration/end condition. **Stacking:** Multiple applications do not compound. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Deafened does not prevent the creature from speaking or supplying its own verbal components unless another condition such as Silenced applies. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 matches inability to hear and automatic failure of hearing-required checks. **Explicit integration decisions:** - Operational clarification: 'verbal coordination may fail' means hearing-dependent coordination requirements fail; no generic roll is added. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Future command/audible-coordination features must state whether hearing is required. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 741, definition paragraph 742; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json).

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Frightened
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText: ## Frightened **Preserved Core text:** Disadvantage while source is visible and cannot willingly move closer. **Effect:** While the source of fear is visible/in line of sight, the creature has disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls. While Frightened it cannot willingly move closer to that source. **Application:** Each application records its fear source. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's duration and repeat-save procedure. **Stacking:** Separate fear sources are tracked independently. Disadvantage does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Fear immunity blocks application. Forced movement may move the creature closer because the prohibition is on willing movement. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 specifies disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of fear is within line of sight, and prohibits willingly moving closer. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 745, definition paragraph 746; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json).

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Incapacitated
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText: ## Incapacitated **Preserved Core text:** Cannot take actions or reactions. **Effect:** The creature cannot take an Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. Passive effects continue unless their own rules require consciousness or another condition disables them. Incapacitated by itself does not reduce Speed or prohibit speech. **Application:** Applied by a condition or effect that explicitly says the creature is Incapacitated. **Duration and ending:** Use the parent condition/effect's duration. **Stacking:** Does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Current shared concentration rules end concentration immediately when the creature becomes Incapacitated. A specific effect may preserve a passive benefit through Incapacitation if explicitly stated. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 matches: cannot take actions or reactions. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW integration: Bonus Actions are included in unavailable actions. - Already explicit in CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md: becoming Incapacitated ends concentration. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 749, definition paragraph 750; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json).

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Invisible
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText: ## Invisible **Preserved Core text:** Cannot be seen normally; attacks against it have disadvantage and its attacks have advantage until location is revealed. **Effect:** Cannot be seen normally. Until an observer knows its location, that observer attacks it with disadvantage and it attacks that observer with advantage. Once location is revealed, these Invisible-specific modifiers end for that observer. Do not re-grant them through V6 generic unseen rules solely because it is still Invisible. A special sense actually seeing it bypasses these modifiers. Knowing location is not seeing; effects requiring sight still need sight. **Application:** Only an effect explicitly granting Invisible applies it. **Duration and ending:** Use the granting effect's duration. V6 attacks reveal location upon attacking; resolve the revealing attack first, then observers able to perceive evidence know the location. Independent hiding/concealment uses its own procedure; later broad vision integration must specify losing and regaining location knowledge. Invisible remains visually effective after revelation. **Stacking:** Multiple Invisible effects do not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** A special sense or magic that actually sees the creature removes Invisible's unseen benefits for that observer within that sense's scope. Knowing location is not the same as seeing. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6: impossible to see without special senses or magic; heavily obscured for hiding; location may be detected by noises or tracks; attacks against have disadvantage and own attacks have advantage. **Source conflicts:** - Core explicitly ends the generic attack advantage/disadvantage when location is revealed; V6 states those attack modifiers without that endpoint. Core controls the conflict. **Explicit integration decisions:** - Operational distinction: visibility state and known location are separate. - No generic detection DC, automatic attack-reveal rule or movement-rehide rule is invented here. - Recovered V6: attacking reveals location. NEW timing clarification: resolve that attack before its revelation; Core location endpoint specifically overrides the otherwise-conflicting unseen attack modifiers. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Stealth, sound, tracks, hiding and location-reveal procedure in the vision/stealth pass. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 753, definition paragraph 754; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json).

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Prone
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText: ## Prone **Preserved Core text:** Crawl or stand; melee attackers within 5 ft. have advantage; ranged attackers have disadvantage. **Effect:** Own attacks have disadvantage. Melee attacks against it within 5 feet have advantage; ranged attacks against it have disadvantage at every distance; other attacks beyond 5 feet have disadvantage. Movement requires crawling or standing. Drop Prone without Speed expenditure; standing costs half current Speed, rounded down, requires nonzero Speed and sufficient movement. Crawl costs 2 feet per foot, or 3 in difficult terrain. **Application:** Applied when an effect explicitly knocks a creature Prone or another rule such as Unconscious causes it. **Duration and ending:** Ends when the creature successfully stands or an explicit effect ends Prone. **Stacking:** Does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Prone immunity blocks application. A feature may explicitly ignore Prone attack penalties. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6: only movement is crawl unless standing; own attack rolls have disadvantage; attacks from within 5 feet have advantage, otherwise disadvantage. **Source conflicts:** - For a ranged attack made from within 5 feet, V6 distance-only wording would grant advantage while Core specifically says ranged attackers have disadvantage. Core controls. **Explicit integration decisions:** - Core-vs-V6 conflict resolved in favor of Core for ranged attacks within 5 feet. - Recovered V6 movement: half-Speed standing and 2/3-for-1 crawling. NEW explicit zero-Speed standing prohibition, preventing zero-cost standing while Grappled. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 763, definition paragraph 764; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json).

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Restrained
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText: ## Restrained **Preserved Core text:** Speed 0; attacks against have advantage, own attacks and Dexterity saves have disadvantage. **Effect:** Speed becomes 0 and cannot benefit from Speed bonuses. Attack rolls against the creature have advantage; its own attack rolls and Dexterity saving throws have disadvantage. **Application:** Only an effect explicitly inflicting Restrained applies it. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's printed duration, save or escape rule. If an effect creates a physical restraint and provides no escape procedure, use the existing shared playtest escape procedure only if that source is eligible for it. **Stacking:** Multiple Restrained applications do not compound penalties, but all independently maintained sources must end before the creature is no longer Restrained. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Restrained immunity blocks application. Teleportation does not automatically end a restraint unless it breaks the source relationship or the applying effect says so. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 adds that the creature cannot benefit from bonuses to Speed. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Final generic physical-restraint escape procedure in combat rules. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 767, definition paragraph 768; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json).

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Silenced
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText: ## Silenced **Preserved Core text:** Cannot use verbal components, command words, Chants, or audible coordination. **Effect:** The creature cannot use spell/ability verbal components, command words, Chants, or any feature requiring audible coordination. It may still think, perceive, move, use somatic/nonverbal abilities and use effects that explicitly function without sound. **Application:** Only effects explicitly inflicting Silenced apply it. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's duration/end rule. **Stacking:** Does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** An ability explicitly usable without speech or audible sound is unaffected. Silence immunity blocks application only if explicitly defined. **Explicit integration decisions:** - Clarification: Silenced is not universal mental or magical shutdown. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Specific audible-command features must state whether they require being heard by recipients. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 769, definition paragraph 770; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json).

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Hands and focuses
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Hands and focuses

A buckler straps to one forearm. Its partially available hand can carry a small nonweapon object, but supplies no free S hand, loading hand, second-weapon attack, two-handed weapon support or active focus manipulation. An ordinary shield or tower shield occupies one hand. Soldier Shield Trained is a specific selected-feature exception for its repeating-crossbow/strapped-shield use, with that feature's actual reload requirements.

A two-handed weapon requires both hands when attacking with it. Releasing one grip costs no Action; regripping is part of its next legal use. This does not free a hand already occupied by another object, restraint or incompatible anatomy.

F requires an actual focus legal for the casting source. A hand holding only that focus may manipulate it and supply S for the same cast; the focus itself is not a conflicting object. A weapon, shield, second object, loading requirement or other hand restriction can make that hand unavailable. An item independently serving as both weapon and focus can use this rule only when an actual source authorizes that item as the caster's focus.

A holy symbol may supply F while held, visibly worn or borne on a shield where that casting source permits holy symbols. A worn or shield-borne symbol does not supply a free S hand. V still requires actual audible speech, and neither a focus nor component pouch waives explicitly priced or consumed materials. The component pouch supplies its ordinary storage function; this guide does not give it a new universal F substitution.

The following focus assignments are **new class integration** for actual legal class spells requiring F. They grant no spells or resource pools. Exact class features may override their own focus rules.

| Casting class | Ordinary focus |
|---|---|
| Bard | One actual instrument |
| Cleric, Paladin | Holy symbol |
| Druid, Shaman, Ranger | Druidic focus |
| Mage, Wizard | Arcane focus |
| Mirrorsage | Steel mirror |
| Oracle | Divination token |
| Crimson Agent, Dragoon, Monk, Thief, Tinker | Token for that class |

Soldier and Warrior gain no spellcasting from focus ownership. An ancestry casting token remains ancestry-grant scoped and cannot substitute for a class focus. An explicitly granted ordinary background arcane focus or holy symbol retains its normal equipment function for a casting source already entitled to that focus category.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Weapons and ammunition
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Weapons and ammunition

Use the source table's exact weapon damage, type, properties, cost and weight. Proficiency follows the reviewed [character foundation](CHARACTER_FOUNDATION_TABLES.md), not the source introduction's general statement about most people using simple weapons. A normal proficient attack adds PB once. Normal ability damage follows the attack's actual rules; an item procedure saying no ability damage overrides it for that item.

- **Finesse:** choose STR or DEX for both attack and damage.
- **Thrown:** a thrown melee weapon uses its ordinary melee ability; Finesse can still supply its choice.
- **Heavy:** Small creatures attack with disadvantage. Extending this to Tiny is a new completion.
- **Light:** enables only the actual reviewed Two-Weapon Fighting procedure, not an independent free attack.
- **Reach:** add 5 feet for that weapon's attacks and its actual opportunity-attack reach.
- **Two-handed:** both hands are required for an attack, subject to an explicit feature exception.
- **Versatile:** use the printed alternate damage for an actual two-handed melee attack.
- **Ammunition:** spend one real compatible ammunition unit per attack. Drawing it is part of the attack; non-repeating loading needs an available hand. Using an ammunition weapon in melee is improvised; a sling must be loaded to deal its improvised damage.
- **Loading:** only one ammunition attack per Action, Bonus Action or Reaction, regardless of Extra Attack. This is not one attack per entire turn or round.
- **Range:** the first number is normal range, the second maximum. Beyond normal range gives disadvantage; beyond maximum is illegal. Ordinary close-range ranged-attack rules still apply.

After an encounter, one uninterrupted minute searching accessible locations recovers `floor(eligible ordinary ammunition expended in that encounter / 2)`. Resolve recovery once for that encounter's expended ammunition; another search cannot recover another half. Only physically accessible, intact ordinary ammunition qualifies. Destroyed, consumed, irretrievable or specifically nonrecoverable ammunition does not. Recovered units remain the same physical items and cannot exist in two inventories. Nets and ordinary thrown weapons do not use this half-ammunition rule.

**Ammunition retail units.** A source ammunition bundle remains the ordinary market purchase unit. `unitPriceCp` and `unitWeightLb` are derived inventory/accounting values and do not by themselves guarantee that a merchant sells fractional bundles. If an actual buyer or seller agrees to split a bundle, price the agreed quantity proportionally and apply transaction rounding once to the final transaction. Starting-kit references record one retail bundle and its twenty `grantedUnits`, not twenty bundles.

**Lance.** Attacks against a target within 5 feet have disadvantage. It requires two hands unless mounted; the item supplies no mount or general mounted-combat procedure.

**Net.** A hit restrains a Large-or-smaller creature unless formless; it deals no damage. Its range remains 5/15 feet. The target or a helper within reach can spend an Action on DC 10 STR to free it. Dealing 5 slashing damage to the net against AC 10 destroys it and frees the victim without hurting that victim. When using a net with an Action, Bonus Action or Reaction, make only one attack for that Action/BA/Reaction regardless of normal attack count. Use the reviewed Restrained condition. A missed net remains an actual object at the target location if physically accessible, not an automatically returned weapon.

**Improvised weapon.** Before rolling, the Director may agree that an actual similar object uses an existing weapon's full profile and relevant proficiency. Otherwise it deals 1d4 appropriate physical damage, with no PB absent actual improvised-weapon proficiency. Throwing an object without Thrown, or using a ranged weapon in melee, uses the improvised rule; improvised throwing range is 20/60 feet.

**Silvering.** Silver one weapon or ten ammunition units for 100 gp. This supplies actual silver eligibility only, with no automatic magic tag, attack bonus or damage bonus.

### New class equipment profiles

| Item | Price | Weight | Profile |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Repeating heavy crossbow | 100 gp | 20 lb | Martial ranged; 1d10 piercing; 80/320 feet; Heavy, Two-handed, Ammunition, Repeating 5 |
| Kama | 2 gp | 2 lb | Simple melee; 1d4 slashing; Light |
| Nunchaku | 2 gp | 2 lb | Simple melee; 1d4 bludgeoning; Light |

**Repeating 5:** an internal magazine holds five bolts, replaces Loading, and spends one bolt per attack. An Action with an appropriate free loading hand loads up to five actually carried bolts. No spare-magazine multiplication, free refill or sixth shot. An exact feature such as Tactical Reload can change the action cost without creating ammunition. The ordinary heavy crossbow remains its separate source profile: 50 gp, 18 lb, 1d10 piercing, 100/400 feet and Loading.

The new **Sidearm** tag applies only to dagger, club, light hammer, handaxe and hand crossbow. Soldier's actual sidearm proficiency can therefore use those profiles; the tag supplies no new statistics or general Martial proficiency. Monk/Shaman staff maps to quarterstaff. Symbolic or relic weapons need an actual existing profile. Kama and nunchaku are not automatically Finesse.

## Carrying and containers

Use the reviewed [body and equipment guide](BODY_EQUIPMENT_PLAYTEST.md) for actual pounds, Load, size, casualty transport and melded equipment. Keep known physical mass distinct from Load and Extraction Class. Known-weight-only items use pounds divided by ten as provisional Load. Every item's weight and Load count once, including containers and contents. An inclusive gross value covers only the contents it names; it does not erase unrelated quantities or supplies.

**New small-weight completion.** A genuinely small physical source unit lacking weight uses 0.02 lb, except fluid vials, full antitoxin/perfume/basic-poison vials, candles, focus sprigs/totems, holy emblems, sealing wax and soap use 0.1 lb. An ink bottle also uses the small-fluid-container 0.1-lb profile. Narrative background small tokens use the separately stated 0.1-lb accessory profile. Record these as operational estimates, keeping the original source weight null. Larger unweighed items, mounts, vehicles and services do not use this fallback. Do not round away accumulated small items. Coins of every ordinary denomination use fifty coins per pound as a new game-weight convention.

The following **new content capacities** exclude the empty container's own weight. Both weight and volume constraints apply where both are given, along with actual shape, closure and access.

| Container | Maximum contents |
|---|---|
| Backpack or sack | 30 lb and 1 cubic foot |
| Pouch | 6 lb and 0.2 cubic feet |
| Component pouch | 6 lb and 0.2 cubic feet |
| Chest | 300 lb and 12 cubic feet |
| Barrel | 500 lb and 40 gallons |
| Basket | 40 lb and 2 cubic feet |
| Bucket | 3 gallons |
| Glass bottle | 1.5 pints |
| Flask | 1 pint |
| Iron pot | 1 gallon |
| Waterskin | 4 pints |

Water uses 1 lb per pint for this game procedure. A waterskin is 1 lb empty plus up to 4 lb water, matching its source 5 lb full value. Do not add that water to the full value a second time. A printed full potion/vial weight includes contents; separately measured contents replace rather than duplicate its covered gross amount.

The component pouch retains its own source weight of 2 lb and price of 25 gp. Its capacity is mundane storage only, with no universal F substitution, automatic materials, costly-component waiver or spell access.

Preserve the source alchemical capacities: glass or crystal vial one dose; alchemist's bottle three doses; reinforced flask five doses; potion belt six actual vials; potion case twelve actual vials. The belt/case also has its printed empty weight. Extra capacity never creates doses, waives ingestion Actions or makes a multi-dose bottle into multiple physical bottles.

The seven packs expand into exactly their source contents at their source package price, not a forced sum of individual retail prices. They have no extra phantom pack-body weight beyond the named backpack/chest. A pack price does not assert that every item is inside that container or waive its capacity: record legal internal storage, external attachment or another actual custody arrangement. An external rope is still carried weight. Rations provide daily food, not full abstract Supply; Goodberry, Jungle Survival and created water retain their reviewed limited food/water effects.
