# Bodies equipment and carrying

**REVIEWED — authored tabletop body, equipment, carrying and continuous meld procedures.** New integration mechanics remain explicitly provisional; runtime implementation is pending. These procedures connect the [Druid form rules](FORM_TEMP_HP_PLAYTEST.md) and [transformation spells](TRANSFORMATION_SPELL_PLAYTEST.md). They apply to the same character, HP record and physical belongings throughout a change. They grant no additional forms, spell access, actions or resources. The approved books remain preserved.

## Entering and changing forms

Before paying for a voluntary change, choose a legal form and size, check its space at your current position, and identify any equipment that must be dropped. If the destination or required drops are illegal, the change does not begin and spends nothing. Otherwise pay the source's normal costs and resolve its actual entry effects once. A successful hostile or forced transformation cannot be prevented merely by excess gear: resolve it under its source rules, then reconcile excess equipment by keeping it external, dropping it or recording pending placement. Other source requirements still apply.

Your Druid form uses your own HP, ability scores, saves, proficiency and conditions. It supplies only its printed anatomy and features. Speech does not imply hands: none of the 26 current Druid profiles grants ordinary hand-based equipment use. Of the 12 spell profiles, only Humanoid grants hands. Each profile retains its exact size and movement permissions.

| Change | Equipment procedure |
|---|---|
| Root body to first Druid form | Record and meld the equipment physically worn, held or carried by your body, including carried containers and their contents. |
| Druid form to another Druid form | Keep the same original melded equipment. End the former form's dependent effects and start the new form under its normal rules. Reconcile newly acquired external items with the new anatomy. |
| A successful spell replaces a Druid or spell form | Close the former transformation and capture the legitimate resulting gear under the new spell's meld rules in one continuous change. There is no moment when you can use the returning equipment. |
| Shapechange changes its current spell profile | Keep compatible external items. Drop incompatible external items; they do not join the original melded equipment. |
| Suppression | Follow the spell's suppression procedure. It is not an ending or a fresh capture of equipment. Original melded gear stays inaccessible. |
| Final reversion, expiry or forced ending | Return to root anatomy, end the source's dependent effects and reconcile surviving equipment as described below. |

The continuing meld record across Druid-to-Druid changes is a **new provisional integration rule**. It prevents shifting from opening an equipment-use window between forms. A spell replacement retains the already-reviewed close-and-capture procedure.

## What melds

Record where each item was before the first change: worn in a particular slot, held in a particular hand, or carried in a particular container or on the body. Ownership alone is insufficient. A sword stored in a wagon stays in the wagon when its owner becomes a Hawk. A legitimately borrowed sword in your actual custody can meld and return normally; the lender remains its owner. Changing ownership metadata does not itself move an inaccessible physical item.

A backpack and each of its contents remain distinct items. Count each item's own weight or Load once; a container does not erase its contents. Melded items remain in your custody but are inaccessible. You cannot withdraw or add contents, use components, consume supplies, fire ammunition or activate equipment through the meld.

Melding never repairs damage, reloads a weapon, restores charges, replenishes supplies or creates a replacement item. Destruction, consumption and legitimate transfers remain real. Keep the current condition and quantity of each actual item.

## Using equipment in a form

| Item or effect | Rule |
|---|---|
| Original armor and shield | Melded and unusable. Exclude their worn or held AC benefits from the form's normal AC. |
| Held weapon, tool, focus or material component | Requires actual access and the appropriate anatomy. A form without hands receives no general permission to use it. |
| Effect requiring an item to be worn, held or equipped | Suspended while the item is melded. |
| Effect requiring only possession or attunement | May continue only when its exact rule is independent of the lost anatomy and physical use. An unspecified magic bonus is not automatically operative. |
| Newly acquired armor, harness, collar or container | Must fit the actual size and anatomy and have a legal way to remain attached or carried. Hands are required for held items, not automatically for every wearable item. |
| Newly acquired external gear when the form changes | Remains external if compatible. Otherwise use the normal drop procedure. It does not silently join an existing meld record. |

The possession-versus-use distinction and individual compatibility checks are **new provisional defaults**. A specific item or form can supply an explicit exception. Do not infer one from a creature's name, appearance or ability to speak. Item-specific compatibility across the full equipment catalog remains to be authored.

## Returning equipment

Resolve a final reversion in this order:

1. Keep current external items that still exist and remain legally equipped or carried by the root body.
2. Return each surviving melded item that remains in the character's legitimate custody to its recorded former slot or container, if available and legal.
3. If an external item now occupies that slot, leave it there. Return the former item as carried inventory if there is a legal place and sufficient capacity.
4. Drop an item that cannot be carried or equipped at the current position or the nearest legal adjacent item position.
5. If no legal drop position exists, record that item's placement as pending. It continues to exist; it is not duplicated, destroyed or used to displace another creature.

Current external equipment taking priority over a former slot is a **new provisional integration rule**. A returned sword may go into available carried storage instead of replacing a sword you actually acquired and equipped during the transformation. Both retain their current condition and ownership.

Destroyed, consumed, physically transferred, lost or otherwise unavailable items never reappear. An item in another custodian's possession cannot return merely because you still claim ownership of it. Someone else's legal ownership does not prevent an intact borrowed item from returning to your continuing legitimate custody.

## Placement and involuntary endings

A transformation does not grant movement. A voluntary size change keeps the same spatial anchor and must fit before payment. Preserve the existing footprint on a same-size change when possible.

A mandatory ending still occurs if the root anatomy does not fit. First try its normal space at the same position, then a legal squeeze under the [movement rules](COMBAT_ACTION_PLAYTEST.md). If neither fits, record a placement conflict. The **new provisional placement procedure** permits only a nearest legal adjacent placement in the same unobstructed region. It cannot pass through a wall, closed barrier or occupied space. Choose the minimum displacement that fits the whole body; among ties, preserve the greatest overlap with its previous footprint. If still tied, the Director uses a fixed neutral board order, not a tactical choice by the affected player. If no adjacent candidate fits, the conflict remains until the obstruction is removed or a legal relocation effect resolves it. Do not search farther afield.

This mandatory normalization spends no movement and triggers no opportunity attack, charge distance, movement benefit or other movement rider. It changes no remaining movement allowance and grants no invented crushing damage. It does not permit a voluntary form change to bypass its preflight.

Track actual height and terrain. Losing flight while unsupported starts ordinary falling from the current location; reversion never moves the creature directly to the ground. Ending a burrowing form underground does not move the creature to the surface. Master of Vermin's permission to pass through Tiny gaps changes clearance, not its printed size.

Use the actual space of the expressed anatomy:

| Size | Space | On a grid of 2.5-foot subcells |
|---|---|---|
| Tiny | 2.5 by 2.5 feet | 1 subcell |
| Small | 5 by 5 feet | 2 by 2 subcells |
| Medium | 5 by 5 feet | 2 by 2 subcells |
| Large | 10 by 10 feet | 4 by 4 subcells |

V6 explicitly supplies Tiny and Medium space. Small and Large complete this bounded table provisionally; the supplied V6 passage does not separately list them. Size category still matters even when two sizes occupy the same space. Squeezing changes clearance and its penalties; it does not change size, carrying capacity or weight. Exact Tiny occupancy requires subcells or equivalent measurement, not treating Tiny as Medium.

## Body weight and conditions

**New provisional rule:** a creature-form transformation preserves the body's existing base physical weight unless an exact rule changes it. Size alone does not change weight. A 180-pound character therefore remains 180 pounds as a Tiny Hawk or Large Bear. This is a magical transformation rule, not a claim about the weight of ordinary animals. It applies equally to the current 26 Druid and 12 creature-form spell profiles.

Record base body weight separately from equipment and condition effects. Petrified multiplies current body weight by ten once; it does not rewrite the base weight or multiply repeatedly for multiple applications. Ending or changing a form does not cure that condition. Temporary Druid form ends under its existing Incapacitated rule, then Petrified continues to apply to the reverted body. An anatomy permitted to persist keeps its own base weight and the same condition overlay.

True Polymorph object anatomy uses its actual documented output weight. Its output ceiling remains the lower of current effective input weight and earliest recorded origin weight. Include a current applicable weight-changing condition in the input, but never rebase the origin ceiling upward. Equipment, casualty Load and estimated pounds do not establish material available for a transformation. Creature-origin object anatomy has no independent sale, salvage or harvest value.

For another creature, mount, floor or platform supporting you, count your effective body weight plus all actual equipment in your custody, including melded items, once. For your own inventory capacity, count what you carry, not your own body weight. Conditions change only the items or body their exact rules affect.

## Carrying and Load

Use pounds for actual weight and Load for inventory burden. Extraction Class describes cargo danger and attention. A casualty's Load describes the difficulty of transporting a body; it is not the body's weight. These quantities answer different questions and never convert automatically into each other.

The following is a **new provisional reconciliation** of V6 physical handling with the staged Gameplay Loop inventory rules. It does not promote the historical Gameplay Loop file into the approved books. V6's optional encumbrance variant remains preserved as an alternative; do not add its penalties to this Load procedure.

| Carrier size | Physical carry limit in pounds | Push, drag or lift limit in pounds | Inventory capacity in Load | Casualty Load for a body of this size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tiny | Strength score × 7.5 | Strength score × 15 | Strength score ÷ 2 | 1.5 |
| Small | Strength score × 15 | Strength score × 30 | Maximum of 0 and Strength score − 2 | 3 |
| Medium | Strength score × 15 | Strength score × 30 | Strength score | 6 |
| Large | Strength score × 30 | Strength score × 60 | Strength score × 2 | 12 |

Use the character's current Strength score, not the modifier or an imported monster score. Tiny's Inventory capacity and casualty Load are new provisional additions. The pound limits come from V6; Small, Medium and Large Load values come from the Gameplay Loop. Larger unsupported transport sizes require their own completed rule before this table can handle them.

Keep fractional Loads without rounding. An item with a printed Load uses that value. If it has only a known weight, its **provisional Load is pounds divided by ten**. A Load-only item may use ten pounds per Load as a clearly labeled estimate for ordinary hauling; this is insufficient for effects requiring documented physical mass.

Count a container's own empty Load plus the contents' Loads, unless an explicitly inclusive Load already covers those exact contents. Handle pounds separately: sum the empty container weight and contents' weights, or use an explicitly inclusive gross weight for the contents it covers. An inclusive Load does not make a printed weight inclusive, or vice versa. Apply this rule through nested containers and meld budgets so every item counts exactly once in each quantity.

With positive carried Load at or above half capacity and no greater than capacity, you are **Burdened**: reduce Speed by 10 feet and apply disadvantage to checks to climb, swim or move silently. An empty inventory is not Burdened, including at zero capacity. Above capacity, that inventory cannot be carried routinely; drop or transfer something, or use a legal alternative such as dragging or a vehicle. These threshold and zero-Load details are provisional clarifications.

Apply actual physical limits when handling a known weight. Between physical carry capacity and twice that capacity, pushing or dragging uses the lower of otherwise-current Speed and 5 feet. A Speed of 0 stays 0; a Speed of 3 stays 3. Lifting does not independently permit movement: moving while supporting a weight must satisfy carrying, pushing, dragging or another exact rule. An anatomy restriction, such as Hawk's prohibition on carrying a Medium ally, still applies even if numbers would fit. Burden penalties do not create hands, harnesses, lift or access to melded gear.

Transporting a creature must pass both checks: the carrier can physically handle the body's effective weight and associated equipment, and can accommodate the casualty Load plus the equipment's Load. Petrified multiplies the body weight by ten, not its casualty Load. Removing gear can reduce equipment weight and Load; it cannot reduce the body's weight or erase its condition.

## Meld limits across repeated transformations

**New provisional meld exception:** legally melded gear is excluded from both your transformed body's active Inventory Load and its own active pound-carrying limit. Record its full Load and weight separately while it remains inaccessible. New external equipment uses the expressed form's current capacities and still needs compatible anatomy and custody.

A **continuous meld chain** begins when root anatomy first enters a transformation that melds gear. At that instant, record two fixed ceilings: the pre-transformation body's ordinary active Load capacity and its ordinary physical carrying capacity in pounds. Legally melded gear must fit both. Keep the actual total Load and pounds of the hidden gear, counting containers and contents once in each quantity.

Druid-to-Druid changes, internal Shapechange switches, suppression, permanent True Polymorph and continuous replacement by another spell do not end the chain or increase its ceilings. Later changes to size or Strength neither increase nor retroactively shrink these historical ceilings. An existing item is not expelled merely to make room for a new one.

A later spell replacement may capture an external item only if the whole item fits the remaining room under **both** ceilings. Do not partially meld an item unless its source defines a divisible cargo quantity. A new item that will not fit remains external if compatible with the destination and within its current carrying limits; otherwise drop it or, for a forced resolution without legal placement, record its placement as pending. Excess cargo never grants immunity to a hostile or forced transformation. Druid-to-Druid changes continue to preserve their existing meld and never recapture external cargo.

For a voluntary change, declare and preflight the full item disposition before spending costs. A successful hostile or forced change resolves its mandatory custody consequences without deleting items or refunding its costs. This same overflow procedure applies at the first forced transformation if the target began with excess cargo; only gear within both starting ceilings can become hidden.

When someone else carries the transformed character, count its casualty Load plus both its melded and external equipment Load. Count the effective physical body weight plus all that equipment for actual weight handling. Melding therefore provides no weightless cargo for another carrier.

Only an actual final return to root anatomy, with the hidden equipment released and reconciled, ends the chain. Returned gear rejoins active inventory under the root body's **current** capacities. Resolve excess with the return-and-drop procedure; overload cannot prevent a mandatory reversion. A later new transformation can then establish a new pair of ceilings from its actual legal starting state.

## Extraction Class and Secure Cargo

Extraction Class is a danger and logistics rating, not a carrying allowance:

| Class | Cargo |
|---|---|
| 0 | Ordinary trade goods |
| 1 | Common monster parts or durable salvage |
| 2 | Uncommon, fragile or regulated cargo |
| 3 | Rare artifacts, volatile substances or living captives |
| 4 | Very rare strategic cargo or dangerous curses |
| 5 | Epic cargo likely to attract sovereign or faction intervention |
| 6 | Legendary cargo requiring a dedicated extraction operation |

Retain relevant Fragile, Volatile, Cursed, Living, Contraband, Perishable and Attention tags. A light object can carry a high Extraction Class, and a heavy ordinary crate can remain Class 0.

**New provisional wording for Secure Cargo:** spend an Action on one legal attach, lift, transfer or protective operation involving one discrete cargo unit or bundle with an assigned Extraction Class. The unit must be physically handleable as declared; naming an entire convoy a bundle does not make it one operation. The action grants no extra capacity, hands, equipment, automatic success, invulnerability or reduction in Extraction Class. Apply actual restraints, harnesses, checks, hazards and source-specific handling requirements.

## Examples

**The remote sword.** A Druid wears armor, holds a staff and carries a pack containing two potions. A spare sword is in a wagon. The armor, staff, pack and both potions meld when the Druid changes. The sword remains in the wagon. Neither potion can be consumed from the melded pack.

**A compatible harness.** A transformed creature acquires a harness made for its present anatomy. A later change checks the harness against the destination form. If it does not fit, the voluntary change requires a legal drop. The harness is neither erased nor added to the old melded equipment.

**The crowded hand.** A spell Humanoid acquires and holds a new weapon. When the spell ends, root anatomy can keep that weapon if legal. The original melded weapon returns to an available legal carrying position, or is dropped if necessary. It does not replace or duplicate the new weapon.

**The loaded Hawk.** A Strength 9 Druid becomes Tiny with 3 Load of legally melded gear. It stays inaccessible and uses neither of the Hawk's active carrying capacities. Tiny capacity is 4.5 Load and 67.5 pounds. An additional package of 3 Load and 30 pounds in a genuinely compatible external carrying arrangement fits both capacities, but exceeds half the Load capacity of 2.25 and makes the Druid Burdened. A rescuer carrying that Hawk counts 1.5 casualty Load plus all 6 Load of equipment, totaling 7.5 Load, and separately satisfies the full body and equipment weight.

**The repeated replacement.** A Strength 9 Medium character starts a chain with 8 Load and 80 pounds of legal gear. The fixed ceilings are 9 Load and 135 pounds. The remaining hidden capacity is therefore 1 Load and 55 pounds. A later spell cannot hide a new 3-Load, 30-pound package even if the current form can carry it externally. A whole 0.5-Load, 50-pound item fits both remaining ceilings; a 0.5-Load, 60-pound item fails the pound limit. Changing form or casting again does not refresh either ceiling.

**The stone casualty.** A Medium ally has a documented base weight of 180 pounds and becomes Petrified. The body now weighs 1,800 pounds but still contributes 6 casualty Load. A Strength 18 Medium rescuer can normally carry 270 pounds or push, drag or lift 540 pounds, so cannot move that body alone through these ordinary procedures, even with enough spare Load capacity. Additional gear is counted separately.

## Source decisions and implementation status

The [first body and equipment conference](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_BODY_EQUIPMENT_CONFERENCE.md) supplies the equipment procedures. The [additional exact evidence](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/CODEX_TEMPORAL_CARRYING_EVIDENCE.md) and [GPT's completed reconciliation](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_CARRYING_RECONCILIATION.md) preserve the V6, Gameplay Loop and Core conflicts and their dispositions. The corrected candidate above replaces the first conference's full-cell Tiny footprint, factor-four mass proposal and automatic active Load from melded equipment. The manuscript review's chain budgets, pound exemption, borrowed-custody correction, separate inclusive quantities and neutral placement tie rule are applied here. [GPT confirmed this exact revised manuscript and its six examples](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_BODY_FINAL_AND_ABJURATION_CONFERENCE.md); the [review manifest](BODY_EQUIPMENT_REVIEW_STATUS.json) records its scope.

The current Druid helper does not yet update the shared body, equipment custody or geometry. The spell helper's coarse hands check does not implement the full compatibility procedure. The finite ground-plane temporal helper does not model elevation, burrowing or Tiny subcells. The authored rules and these implementation gaps are separate; none of them enables full Time Loop or closes the whole-game review.

# Creature companions: life, commands and identity

**REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED: 121 targeted checks and 2,800 Ranger conversion states.** This overlay discusses 100 exact passages from Druid, Mage, Mirrorsage, Ranger and Wizard, supported by five frozen common paragraphs. It closes no full class, form, temporary-HP system or complete runtime by itself. [Source register](CREATURE_LIFECYCLE_SOURCE_BINDINGS.md), [source integrity](CREATURE_LIFECYCLE_SOURCE_VALIDATION.json), [behavior checks](CREATURE_LIFECYCLE_PLAYTEST_VALIDATION.json).

The original class cards and frozen class guide remain intact. The notebook's first classification, boundary reconciliation and event-model decisions are preserved in the audit folder. Where the historical first reply differs from the later boundary replies, the later explicit resolution controls. In particular, Auto-Raise is automatic, its new minion cannot act at all in the creation round, and Mirrorsage Charm was not in the older 219-source control closure.

## At the table

Keep one companion command and one offensive companion allowance per owner per numbered round, including multiclass companions and devices. A normal command costs your Bonus Action. A damaging companion action, or Mage/Wizard control action, spends the offensive allowance. A pure support command spends only the command. The earlier device ledger's internal field named `damage` now represents this shared offensive allowance; its public behavior remains compatible with existing device checks.

Issue ordinary commands during your regular turn. The selected companion moves and performs its command immediately after your whole turn, in an attached phase. It receives no extra independent turn. If it or its target becomes ineligible before execution, the command fails without refund. Your later incapacity or removal alone does not cancel an issued command; actual concentration/source ending can. Uncommanded companions can move defensively and Dodge, subject to their conditions; this grants no generic Reaction or autonomous attack/control.

Use the owner's original regular companion markers for recharge and previous/next-turn references. Extra turns, initiative changes and removal do not restart those markers. The attached phase's event-resolution checkpoint is distinct: it refreshes no Reaction, recharge, Action, death save or regular duration clock.

## Different kinds of creature life

| Creature | HP and 0 HP | Return and identity |
|---|---|---|
| Finite standard summons, Druid swarms, Mage Familiar, Mirror Beasts | HP-only bounded layer; at 0 disappear/end | No corpse, resource or free resummon; a new summon pays its actual source costs |
| Ranger Beast | HP-only; **NEW** immediate death at 0, no Wound checks, Stable or death saves | Actual animal and ordinary surviving corpse; death ends bond. No automatic resurrection or rebond |
| Mage Lich elite | Destroyed bound asset at 0; no usable corpse/resources | Same unique asset remains owned. Soulbound or actual completed LR can return it |
| Wizard standard undead | Destroyed at 0; consumed body never returns as new fuel | Ends on destruction, dismissal or owner's next completed LR, including Auto-Raised minions |
| Wizard elite | Supplied profile/cap only in this package | Binding/acquisition and return procedure are still missing; no create/bind/return API |
| Reflective Companion | Original creature's HP and life rules | Temporary control relation; no copied body, reset, new statistics or duplicate turn |
| Druid form | Same character's HP/life rules | Full forms and Buffer Reserve remain a separate open interface |

Companion healing restores legal normal HP only. It does not reset identity, duration, recharge, actions, source uses, effects or command budgets. Ranger's “heal normally” supplies no Hit Dice pool or automatic rest healing. The HP-only layer is specific to this reviewed companion chassis, not generic law for all animals/NPCs. Existing animal conditions, disease, poison, explicit injuries and timed effects survive bonding.

## Stats and ownership

**NEW:** finite created creatures snapshot base HP and AC at creation. Attacks, saves, class DC and S use the current values of the original source owner at resolution. Keep source owner, current controller, source class and creation source separate. A temporary controller does not donate their class levels, PB or attack bonus. The implementation rejects stats belonging to another owner/class; it provides no unrestricted transfer/rebinding operation.

Standard profile: AC 12 + floor(PB/2), HP 2L, Speed 30, owner PB for saves, one class attack for S d6 with printed melee/ranged mode. Druid swarm uses current PB+WIS, piercing and its printed tiny-gap movement. Familiar snapshots AC 12+PB and HP 5+Mage level+M; its current source-owner Mage attack fires a 30-foot Elemental Dart for S d4. Focus is fixed at creation: Lightning adds Fly30, Fire/Cold their matching resistance. Changing Focus neither morphs nor refills it. One Familiar; replacement ends the prior one.

Ranger maximum is **NEW dynamic** max(1, 2×current Ranger level + actual WIS modifier), not M. Current PB updates its standard AC/saves/attack. Persistent Mage elite maxima use current source-owner Mage level; fixed AC stays fixed. Capacity growth never heals; shrink clamps HP without damage. Wizard elite profiles use the same names with their own original Wizard source statistics if a future legitimate binding source establishes them.

The [reviewed maximum-HP ledger](MAXIMUM_HP_PLAYTEST.md) supplies source-qualified modifiers. Conjuration is the original creating Wizard level snapshot and requires actual Wizard spell creation. Corpse Harvest qualifies only with actual access; Auto-Raise is not a spell and grants no new Conjuration snapshot. Flesh Ascendant is the explicit dynamic eligible-current-controller exception; engine and card are one effect, not two bonuses. Creation starts at full final legal maximum unless the actual source enters damaged; later added capacity never fills HP. Callers update dynamic modifier records from their real sources.

## Ranger's persistent bond

Use the printed one-hour ritual, touch, 4 RP and one long-rest use. The animal must already be willing/tamed, noncorrupted, INT below7 and CR no greater than Ranger level. The helper does not invent finding/taming rules. Keep one chosen movement mode, capped40 feet, and the original keen-sense identity; no monster stat block, boss powers or free special actions. Exact keen-sense selection definitions remain an evidence gap.

**NEW initial conversion:** for a living animal, new HP = max(1, floor(new maximum × old current HP / old maximum)). A wounded animal stays proportionally wounded. This is profile conversion, not healing or damage. A living bound Beast cannot be rebonded to refill HP. On death, ordinary legal resurrection may restore the same animal under its own source, but it remains unbonded. A new full ritual also requires an actual completed long rest after bond death.

Physical body identity is separate from current corpse eligibility. Keep one record whose state is living, corpse, consumed or removed. Accepting an already-resolved, independently legal resurrection immediately marks that same body living and unavailable as a corpse, before any rebond. Corpse Gateway cannot use it while living. A later genuine death with a surviving body makes that same record a corpse again; no fragment/new body identity is generated. A consumed/removed body requires explicit reconstruction by the actual resurrection source before it can return. The notification helper grants no resurrection ability, payment exemption or automatic bond. Rebond uses the actual post-resurrection HP ratio and preserves death history; it cannot claim a healthier ratio. Full global corpse decay/cleanup remains open.

## Mage Lich assets and elite commands

An actual successful Lich transformation unlocks Boneflayer, Dreadblade and Wraithbound. Readiness and informed retirement-risk consent are source guards; this lifecycle helper does not perform that irreversible ritual. **NEW shared identity:** across Mage/Wizard, one owner can have at most one of each named elite and three total. Destroyed assets still occupy those identities. Any future external Wizard binding must validate against the same asset register; the current helper offers only its profile schema.

| Elite | Profile | Source-native actions/riders |
|---|---|---|
| Boneflayer | AC14, HP12+2L, Speed30; ranged60, 2d6+S necrotic | Fear Pulse replaces attack, enemies10 feet WIS or Frightened through target-next-end, recharge3. Grave Miasma replaces attack: radius10 point30 until next owner-start, enemies entry/start1d6 once, recharge3 |
| Dreadblade | AC16, HP16+3L, Speed30; melee5, 1d8+S necrotic | Concentrating hit target immediately saves with disadvantage; natural20 applies printed −1 attack Weakened until target-next-end. Advantage against forced movement |
| Wraithbound | AC14, HP10+2L, Fly40/hover; melee5, 1d8+S necrotic | Natural20 CON or Stunned until target-next-end under shared character→target hard-denial guard |

Rolls, chosen enemy geometry, recharge payments, exact condition applications and canonical hard-guard sharing remain caller/source responsibilities. This helper returns attack profiles and bounded lifecycle/command transitions; it does not silently execute every on-hit effect.

**NEW Miasma integration:** creation spends one offensive command. Its native finite entry/start damage needs no second command and does not spend next round's offense. Retain no-resource/no-recursion flags. An old zone tick is not a new companion turn or attack.

Wraithbound loses source invisibility on attack **or control**. It can regain it at the end of its next original regular companion marker if the predicate remains satisfied. A current-marker end cannot immediately restore it. The actual offense event must notify its marker state. Core Invisible still does not grant unknown location, sight through walls or automatic target legality.

Soulbound requires the destroyed own bound elite within30 or its inert token, legal empty space30, Action, 5 RP and one LR use. Return the same asset/instance at **NEW source-specific** max(1, floor(current maximum/2)), plus S+M temp HP for60 seconds under normal temp-HP rules. Do not copy machine reconstruction permissions. Preserve spent uses, recharge clocks, command history and still-applicable effects. Completed LR returns those same Mage assets at full current HP unless an actual campaign consequence prevents it. Rest-use/recharge resets come only from the canonical rest system; a return itself grants none. Natural effect expiries must still be processed.

## Wizard corpses, standard minions and Auto-Raise

Corpse Harvest costs Action+4 RP, recharge2, legal corpse/space30. Humanoids qualify; actual Infernal Pact also permits Fiends. Skeleton: AC14, HP6+2WizardL, Speed30, ranged30 1d6+S necrotic. Zombie: AC12, HP10+3L, Speed20, melee5 1d8+S. Goblin Thrall: AC13, HP8+2L, Speed30, melee5 1d6+S; requires a goblinoid body even with Pact.

All standard minions and reserved Auto-Raise slots share a cap of3. Manually dismiss an existing standard minion before attempting a fourth; failed creation spends nothing and does not consume the body. Harvest consumes the original body. Summoned, raised, copied, illusory or fragmented remains provide no new corpse fuel. Corpse Gateway uses a legal body without consuming it; it does not grant raising permission. Global corpse decay/removal rules remain open.

Ghoul Lash uses the shared BA command and2 RP with another controlled undead within5 at issuance. Its chosen standard minion makes **two independently rolled normal attacks**, not numerical damage copies. Each can miss/hit/crit. This remains one command and one offensive allowance, with at most one Auto-Raise opportunity.

**NEW queue integration, preserving the printed automatic trigger:** the first qualifying personal killing blow by a standard minion automatically reserves the body, one capacity slot and the killer's mechanical minion type. It spends the owner's round opportunity immediately. Ineligible kills do not spend it; a qualifying trigger cannot voluntarily be declined. Body reservation does not prevent another legal consumer from taking the body first. A destroyed/expired killer does not cancel an already-created reservation.

Resolve after immediate death responses and already-due end damage/saves, before ordinary expiry cleanup, in stable application order. An ordinary attached attack has its own `attachedCompanionEnd` queue checkpoint after its consequences, in the same numbered round. That checkpoint is not a second regular turn marker. Kills before the checkpoint closes may reserve. A later administrative kill cannot reopen it, roll forward or leave an orphan queue; its unused opportunity remains unused unless another independently valid trigger occurs before another legally open checkpoint.

At resolution, still-eligible body, legal space and cap permit creation; otherwise release the reservation but retain the spent round use. Auto-Raise costs no Action or RP. The newborn cannot voluntarily move, Dodge, support, attack, control or react in its creation numbered round. Passive defenses/conditions/expiry continue. It ends at destruction, dismissal or next completed owner LR. Owner unconsciousness/death alone does not invent a new ending.

## Mirror Beast, Reflective Companion and Echo origin

One Mirror Beast **or** Reflective Companion slot. Summoning a Beast replaces the old body/control relation administratively; it never kills the real previously controlled target. Mirrorcall adds M max/current HP at creation and5 Speed. Advanced Mirrorcall spends BA once/encounter for appearance plus its printed swim/climb adjustment; Mirror Shift spends BA+1 RP/recharge2 for swim30 or climb30. Neither heals, restores uses, releases Echoes, grants flight/anatomy, or refreshes duration. Corrupted and Shattered on-hit dice/splash retain their exact once-round source qualifiers; full damage-event execution remains in the later copy/trigger work. Luminant Bond supplies only its printed local WIS-save/Invisible advantage interface, with ordinary cover/targeting intact.

Ordinary Beast: Action2 RP, empty space15, one minute, recharge3. Radiant/Shattered: Action4 RP, empty space15, concentration3 of the owner's regular turns, recharge4. Actual scheduler supplies the precise three-turn endpoint. Radiant chooses attack, BA+1 RP heal S d4 to living ally5, or paid Echo origin, once per numbered round. The healing pipeline resolves rolls/modifiers before the lifecycle HP gain; no invented resurrection.

**NEW Mirror-origin exception:** your Echo resolves immediately as your Action during your own turn, including a real extra own turn if real Action, BA and unused shared caps exist. An extra Action alone supplies no BA. Preflight active Beast, actual record, release cap, owner target perception, current Beast range/LOE, Action, BA and RP before any spend. The Beast grants no remote sensory feed or free preceding movement. You own record consumption, Dissonance, Refrain, concentration and spell damage. BA command is spent; offensive companion allowance is not. A later independently legal Gadget Sync may spend it. No second BA command or second local Beast option appears.

Charm Creature remains Action3 RP, one LR use, WIS save, target INT<=6 within30, concentration at most3 rounds, no PC/boss without actual encounter permission. Repeat save at target's actual turn end and when harmed by your side. No suicide, compelled beliefs or permanent allegiance. Original identity/HP/conditions/effects/stat provenance/initiative remain unchanged. A successful save spends cast costs but does not replace an existing Beast. Source-specific save/Charm immunity and permitted target/route checks remain caller responsibilities.

**NEW hard-denial reconciliation:** initial Charm applies the actual Charmed relation and slot without spending hard denial. While active, one BA may queue at most one pending forced ordinary Action, never unique powers; ordinary attack damage capped S d6. Queue to the next future regular target Action: this round if upcoming, next round if already passed. Pay BA in issue round; reserve offensive allowance in the resolution round. The target receives no duplicate attached turn.

At the designated Action slot, revalidate Charm, capability, legal order and the shared character→target→encounter hard guard. Valid execution replaces that Action and spends both hard guard and offense. If Charm ends, target becomes incapable, legality fails or another same-character feature spends hard denial, cancel and release unused offense; retain BA/costs and do not spend an additional hard denial. Call the pending-order revalidation when those facts change, not only at the future turn. Once a forced Action has occurred, this effect permits no further forced attack, Dodge, movement or replacement Action. Actual Charmed restrictions/repeat saves remain; no new fallback is invented.

## Druid summon dependencies

Base Swarm Summoning: Action, one SR use, space30, concentration10 minutes; independent of form. Carrion Rat King: Action, actual Form Surge, once per shift, one standard swarm for at most60 seconds and only while its parent form remains; replacement affects its old form swarm, not independent Base Swarm. Broodmother: on entry actual Form Surge creates two adjacent bodies with one combined commanded attack; end at the earlier of60 seconds or parent form end. Form change ends those children, not unrelated paid summons.

Master of Vermin substitutes the paid summoning spell's profile while preserving its actual count, duration and concentration. No extra casts, creatures or command budget. The helper requires certified source access, legal target/space/range/LOE/perception, ordinary condition capability, real paid Form Surge, canonical action wallets/use scopes, actual concentration/clock endpoints and actual completed rest events. # Devices, Totems and companion commands

**REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED: 132 targeted checks and 1,200 reconfiguration states.** This is the lifecycle and shared-command overlay for 74 supplied Tinker/Shaman passages and three frozen shared paragraphs. It does not certify all effects on those cards, all companions, or the whole game.

The [source register](DEVICE_LIFECYCLE_SOURCE_BINDINGS.md) preserves all exact procedures and hashes. The [source check](DEVICE_LIFECYCLE_SOURCE_VALIDATION.json) and [behavior check](DEVICE_LIFECYCLE_PLAYTEST_VALIDATION.json) cover this bounded package. The other 157 passages in the wider companion inventory are still open. Original sources and the frozen class guide remain unchanged.

The original names, costs, targets, rolls, damage, class gates and frequencies control. A label such as “device,” “deployed” or “support command” below is a classification, not an added ability. **NEW** marks an integration decision explicitly discussed with the notebook.

## At the table

Keep one card/token for each active device, Totem or companion. Record its current HP, expiry, occupied capacity, spent ammunition/uses and protected disablement. A persistent Anacite Drone also retains an ownership identity across reconstruction.

When a device reaches 0 HP, release its active slot and record what destroyed it. A destroyed Drone remains a recoverable machine. Standard summoned companions disappear. Totems stop their aura immediately. Expiry, dismissal, replacement and loss of concentration end effects without producing destruction rewards.

Repair is not reconstruction. Field Repair and Repair Pulse cannot bring a destroyed machine back. Snap Rebuild and the Drone's ten-minute repair can do so under their exact costs, ranges and limits. Snap must still fit the original slot footprint and beat the original expiry.

All companions belonging to one character share one Bonus Action command and one damaging companion action per numbered round. Separate tokens, multiclass companions, an extra Action or an extra turn do not reset those limits.

## Lifecycle and persistent state

Primary state is deployed, retracted, destroyed, expired, ended or replaced. Protected disablement is a separate flag. A disabled Drone can be retracted or destroyed; neither action clears the flag. An active entity functions only while deployed, before its expiry, above 0 HP if it has HP, available in its owner's configuration, and not disabled.

**NEW:** administrative ending releases capacity without destruction, refunds or salvage. Earlier destruction debris can remain after the original timer, but cannot be Snap Rebuilt at or after that timer. Inert remnants do not acquire collision, cover, terrain or repair rights without a source.

The Drone has an asset identity for ownership and configuration and an instance identity for the current physical incarnation. Ordinary repair, retraction, redeployment, Snap and Reconfiguration preserve that instance. A genuinely new paid deployment or explicit long-rest Drone rebuild uses a new instance.

Protected disablement belongs to the persistent Drone asset. A long-rest rebuild can therefore produce a full-HP Drone that remains disabled. The printed automatic clearance is a completed **short rest**; a long rest is not silently substituted for that marker.

## Commands, Reactions and damage allowances

| Event | Shared BA command | Shared damaging action | Other payment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Attack command | Spent | Spent | Printed costs |
| Support-only command | Spent | Available | Printed costs |
| Gadget Sync shot | Unchanged | Spent | Trigger and 1 RP |
| Decoy Dummy destruction damage | Unchanged | Spent if available | Automatic engine trigger |
| Default follow/move/Dodge | Unchanged | Unchanged | No attack granted |
| Emergency Protocols, Protective Programming, Magnetic Wall | Unchanged | Unchanged | Owner's printed Reaction |
| Volatile Components / Cinderflame destruction burst | Unchanged | Unchanged | Their own predicates and limits |

Gadget Sync after support may use the still-unspent damaging allowance. Gadget Sync first leaves a later BA support command available. Neither sequence grants a second damaging activation. Rocket Tower's two-target shot is one activation; Advanced Turret Bay does not command both turrets together.

**NEW scope clarification:** engine[6]'s damaging-trigger limit applies to its deployable profiles, including Decoy. It does not impose that limit on separately printed Volatile Components or Cinderflame. A suppressed Decoy trigger grants no damage and is not banked. An off-turn Decoy trigger still uses the current numbered-round allowance. Tinker BA commands also require their narrower regular-turn eligibility. Other timing/trigger legality is checked by the caller.

Nano Aegis uses a support command for each printed BA+1RP output; it cannot attack with that command. Its reviewed maximum of three outputs remains. Duration extensions do not restore ammo, uses or healing pulses.

## Durability and immunities

| Profile | Maximum / initial HP | AC | Stat timing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Anacite Drone | max(1, 5 + actual INT modifier + Tinker level) | 13 + actual INT modifier | Current actual owner values |
| Ordinary HP-bearing deployable | 2 × Tinker level | 12 + PB | NEW creation snapshot |
| Deployable Expertise on eligible object | Add M maximum/initial HP | Add 1 | Creation; excludes Drones |
| Totem, including Echo | 2 × Shaman level | 12 + PB | NEW placement snapshot |
| Named standard elemental | 2L; Harmony makes 3L | 12 + floor(PB/2) | Creation |
| Elemental Chorus package | 4L; Harmony makes 5L total | 12 + PB | Creation |
| Salvage / Reaper Scrapling | L | 12 | Creation |
| Restoration Field | No HP-bearing anchor | None | Slot effect |

A legitimate temporary actual INT change updates Drone AC, maximum HP and its current PB+INT attack bonus. Increased maximum supplies capacity without healing. Decreased maximum clamps current HP without damage or destruction. Finite created profiles keep their creation statistics.

Harmony adds HP at creation and one source turn of duration, capped at four. It does not heal an existing summon. Chorus is one shared package represented by four spirits. Echo's 10-foot radius and half aura numbers do not halve its durability.

Machines/Totem objects have no organic Wounds, Stable state or death saves. Legal temporary HP is a separate buffer. The Drone's printed poison/psychic and Charmed immunities do not imply every condition immunity. Totems have their own printed poison/psychic and condition immunities. “Vulnerable to ordinary weapon and other damage” means susceptible in this source wording, not an invented numerical doubling.

The reference's damage method receives an amount after all legally applicable defenses. Condition eligibility, object immunities, attack rolls, saves and exact riders remain caller work. A Shaman elemental is a creature companion, not automatically a machine.

Scraplings are temporary companions with their printed stats and shared command rules. Neither supplied Scrapling source establishes generic machine/device targeting. Salvage's slot cost does not grant that category. They disappear at zero HP and do not thereby gain Field Repair, Repair Pulse, protected-disable routing, Recycling, Volatile Components, Snap or other device-only permissions.

## Repair, reconstruction and disabling

| Procedure | Eligible target and change | Payment / limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Field Repair | Touched damaged machine with positive HP; or protected-disabled positive-HP machine, even at full HP. An available carried/retracted Drone qualifies. Restores rolled S d8+M up to max and clears protected disablement | Action, 1 RP, printed Recharge 2 |
| Repair Pulse | Up to three functional friendly devices; restores floor(maxHP/2), applies printed +1 AC until next source start. Does not clear protected disablement | Action, 3 RP, 1/short rest |
| Drone ten-minute reconstruction | Destroyed owned Drone with available original material; restores max(1, floor(maxHP/2)); preserves protected disablement | 10 minutes, 1 RP, 1/short rest |
| Snap Rebuild | Destroyed device/Drone, legal material, original free compatible slot footprint and remaining duration; restores max(1, floor(maxHP/2)); preserves disablement | BA, 2 RP, 1/encounter |
| Disable-clear tools procedure | Clears only protected-disable flag, including on a destroyed persistent machine; restores no HP | Separate 10 minutes, 1 RP, tinker's tools |
| Completed short rest | Clears protected disablement only | Actual completed short-rest marker |
| Long-rest Drone rebuild | Full HP, fresh physical instance for owned asset, even after old material consumed; preserves uncleared asset disablement | Actual source-authorized completed long rest |

**NEW machine viability arithmetic:** explicit half-maximum reconstruction has minimum 1 HP. Repair Pulse on a functional max-1-HP machine still restores floor(1/2) = 0.

The two ten-minute procedures are distinct rights. Reconstructing a disabled, destroyed Drone does not also buy disable clearance. Reconstruction is not a generic cleanse and does not reset ammunition, modules, spent uses, Overdrive history or unexpired legal effects. Normally damage has already consumed temp HP before destruction; this package adds no destroyed-machine temp-HP grant.

Routing Dissonance is the engine[7] BA, once/short rest, up to two current Dissonance into an active device within 30 feet. It creates no RP, does not reset Refrain, and blocks movement, attacks, auras and triggers while the device's timer continues.

## Capacity, placement and dependent Totems

Deployable slots are zero before the engine's class gate, one at Tinker 6, two at 13 and three at 17. Advanced Turret Bay uses two available slots for 4 RP, or its one-slot/2-RP fallback; zero free slots is illegal. Drones use separate persistent ownership capacity, not deployable slots.

At Tinker 13, choose exactly two basic Drones with exactly one module each or exactly one Drone with exactly two distinct modules during the printed configuration procedure. No more than two. Earlier module acquisition remains governed by its own class gates. **NEW:** withdrawing the excess Drone into an unavailable/retracted configuration causes no destruction or salvage.

Totem capacity is one, then two at Shaman 13. **NEW generalization:** an ordinary new Totem placed at capacity replaces a chosen active Totem, including at capacity one. Echo needs a separate free capacity; creating Echo alone never evicts another Totem.

**NEW dependent Echo rule:** ending, replacing, destroying or expiring the parent ends its Echo and releases both capacities. That Echo ending is administrative, not its own destruction. Ending only Echo leaves the parent. Echo shares the parent's remaining duration, concentration and upkeep.

Preflight ownership, source use, space/range, action, resources and capacity before payment or ending anything. Determine all dependent releases first. A valid parent replacement can free room for the new parent plus a separately paid Echo. If Echo cannot fit, its optional creation is unavailable; the caller can submit an ordinary parent-only placement instead. Failure of a submitted combined transaction changes nothing.

All active Totems share their concentration burden. Losing it ends their effects and dependent Echoes without destruction rewards. Totem movement follows its printed BA, 15-foot move through an open route within the printed range; it retains expiry, concentration, recipient ledgers and pulse schedule. Movement grants no entry heal.

## Destruction, debris and source-specific opportunities

Record the instance, original hostile cause, actual enemy hit versus transferred damage, deliberate sacrifice, whether the object itself is a copy, friendly damage, secondary explosion and inherited branch flags at destruction. Separately record whether incoming damage was copied. A real device destroyed by copied damage still has ordinary destruction consequences; only that damage's actual restriction flags suppress them. “Copied object” exclusions do not mean “any object damaged by a copy.”

**NEW anti-loop integration:** the first actual destruction of an instance establishes its only object-linked opportunity and material set. Nonqualifying and declined opportunities are closed for that instance. Snap does not create another set. A second physical destruction still ends the rebuilt device but cannot supply another harvest, Volatile opportunity or material record.

Recycling, Salvage, Reaper and Snap share the usable original material. The first successful consumer spends it. Volatile does not consume material. A source-qualified Volatile can therefore precede one legal material consumer. Declining Volatile on Device A does not spend the owner's round allowance for Device B.

| Source | Important predicate |
| --- | --- |
| Efficient Recycling | Your destroyed non-copy device; not deliberate sacrifice; debris within reach, after combat for one minute, 1/short rest. Refund at most min(1 RP, actual deployment RP). Enemy cause is **not required**. |
| Scrap Salvage | Enemy-destroyed qualifying material; Action+1 RP, 1/encounter; one slot-using Scrapling at printed location |
| Scrap Reaper | Qualifying destroyed enemy-hit device/material within 30 feet; Reaction+2 RP, 1/short rest; printed short-lived Scrapling uses **no deployable slot** |
| Volatile Components | First enemy-caused device destruction; excludes deliberate sacrifice, copy, friendly damage and secondary explosion; enemy within 5 feet; once per owner/round |
| Snap | Original destroyed instance/material, original footprint free and original expiry not reached |

Scraplings cannot spawn their own replacement. Reaper still uses the later BA command and damaging-action budget for its detonation. Its absent slot cost is not inferred from the separate Salvage card. Reaper also carries its source's broader no-own-destruction-chain property; a later type ruling must not silently remove that protection.

Inherited noResourceGeneration blocks Recycling refunds. It does not automatically prohibit all non-resource transformations. Inherited noRetaliation blocks a destruction explosion such as Volatile. Inherited noDeathTriggers blocks Volatile, Cinder's destruction burst and Reaper's destruction-triggered Reaction. It does not automatically prohibit the later Action-based Scrap Salvage or ordinary Recycling. Source-specific exclusions still apply to each consumer.

Cinderflame's qualifying destruction event is captured before its standard-companion disappearance. Its printed burst may then resolve, with the printed three-enemy cap, save, damage and no further death/resource triggers. Dismissal, expiry and concentration ending are not destruction.

Volatile Injection spends M **normal** device HP and requires current HP strictly greater than M. Temp HP cannot pay it. It is not damage or a qualifying destruction event. Deliberate sacrifice sources retain their express no-proc/salvage/copy/refund exclusions.

## Magnetic Wall and existing damage sharing

**NEW source binding and timing integration:** when the printed ranged weapon hit, ally distance and wall-line predicates hold, the owner's Reaction transfers exactly min(remaining defended damage, S+M) to the functional Wall after the ally's ordinary defenses/prevention and before temp HP.

The transfer retains damage type. The Wall branch carries noSecondMitigation and noRetransfer. It receives no second AC roll, critical, attack-hit rider or second mitigation pass. Legal Wall temp HP then normal HP absorb it; reaching zero destroys it and releases its slot.

Enemy damage intercepted this way remains enemy-caused. Choosing the Reaction is not deliberate sacrifice. A Wall destroyed this way may qualify Volatile and a source-qualified material consumer. Transferred damage is not itself an attack hit on the Wall; enemy-hit-only Reaper qualification remains distinct.

Emergency Protocols retains its existing additional noRetaliation flag. Enemy attribution and ordinary debris survive, but destroying the Drone cannot bypass that flag to trigger Volatile. This new Magnetic Wall binding supplements the earlier 39-source redirection package; it was not part of that package's original count.

## Reconfiguration and implementation boundaries

Reconfiguration requires a functional deployed device and a known eligible nonhealing destination. **NEW arithmetic:** newHP = max(1, floor(oldHP × newMaxHP / oldMaxHP)), capped at new max. Preserve instance, slot footprint, expiry, ammunition, spent uses, destruction history and effect clocks. This conversion is neither damage nor healing.

Pending modifiers only apply when their own predicate remains true. Overcharge grants no free command; a profile unable to use it does not refund it or reset its deadline. Exact source access, profile legality and pending-modifier application remain caller responsibilities.

Restoration Field is a slot-using concentration effect with its already-reviewed healing scheduler. Its source supplies no HP, AC or physical anchor. It cannot be attacked as a fabricated machine, repaired, Snap Rebuilt, Remote Detonated, used for Volatile Injection/salvage or targeted by protected Dissonance routing merely because it consumes a slot.

The implementation stores authoritative owner/instance/material identifiers, original ClockMarkers, canonical command ledgers, atomic RP/action payments and explicit source-scoped use keys. The caller must provide the same real owner wallet and ledger across abilities, unique use-scope keys tied to the real rest/encounter calendar, legal source actions and costs, actual targets/geometry, source profiles and class gates. It must also propagate these life states to the pulse/concentration engine.

All timed device effects supplied here expire during a completed long rest, explaining the fresh Drone instance's empty timed-effect list and zero tempHP. This is not a generic reconstruction cleanse: a future permanent or long-rest-surviving source effect must retain its own clock and rules.

This reference does not create a complete runtime transaction manager, movement/collision system, all damage riders, every condition interaction, all 157 remaining companion candidates or a video game. It supplies the same decisions in tabletop prose and a precise checked model for later implementation.

## Discussion evidence

Saved in docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game:

## What is implemented

The reference restores an immutable initiative-start snapshot through a preflighted transaction. It handles a finite development scene containing canonical Core life states, action wallets, selected feat shields, a temporal healing-consumption ledger, explicit Soul Bind/death identities, physical provenance, finite level-ground geometry, reward opportunities, external dependency records and character memory. The existing shared `LifeState`, `Wallet` and `BufferLedger` objects retain their identities. Spent resources and historical event records remain current.

The restore is permitted only after a complete atomic combat event, before round four, with an available Reaction and an unspent actual long-rest use. It never interrupts a damage, healing or command transaction. Preflight checks all registered state, source policies, physical dependencies and placements before charging anything. A prepared plan becomes stale if the registered world changes before commit. The single-thread reference requires the host scene lock through preflight and commit. Each committed restore also retains an engine/Director audit frame with the previous and resulting field values; that audit is never a source of character memory. The existing canonical BufferLedger completed-rest epoch also governs Time Loop's own long-rest use; there is no independent rest counter to diverge.

At commit, encounter initiative and the snapshot's Action/Bonus Action/Reaction allowances, RC and declared per-encounter uses return. Every outstanding Oracle Time Loop Reaction debt overlays the restored budgets. Only the owner's actual normal regular-start refresh clears that owner's debt. The public `TemporalKernel.regular_start(actor, now)` obtains the actor's canonical Wallet internally; it accepts no Wallet argument and rejects actor aliases sharing one Wallet. The bounded scheduler enforces the next actor at the initiative cursor, allows one active regular turn, and advances the cursor/round only when that exact turn ends. An out-of-order or repeated start cannot refresh a Reaction or advance the actual regular marker. Genuine extra turns require the later source adapter and cannot be represented as regular starts. The new iteration has fresh round/turn identities; the rewind itself creates no turn start, pulse or recharge tick. Elapsed world time, real regular-marker count, RP and finite-use history remain unchanged.

## Conservation checks

| State | Bounded behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Core HP and Wounds | Restore numeric snapshot HP against the current legal maximum. A lower maximum clamps HP without damage or healing; a higher maximum does not increase snapshot HP. Critical Wound healing ceilings do not limit temporal assignment. |
| Maximum HP | Use the existing maximum-HP calculation and an exact source-ID temporal policy table. The three reviewed Monk trauma IDs may restore except after actual rest ending. Tough, Tough as Nails, Tenacity and Dark Fortitude use current permanent progression records; temporary endpoints on those passive records are rejected. Other sources, including valid ordinary max-HP sources whose temporal/lifecycle adapter is absent, reject this fixture. Current supported external records overlay the result. Structural progression changes reject without a dedicated adapter. The host supplies current legal base/stat values. |
| Stable recovery | Preserve its original world deadline and event identity. An already resolved or expired recovery cannot replay; this kernel rejects such restoration rather than inventing a recovery rule. |
| Temporary HP | Restore the same grant ID and original snapshot amount only while its source's deadline/rest epoch/entity dependency remains valid. Supported IDs are Chef, Inspiring Leader, Field Medic, Soul Cage, Empowered Summoning and Blood Ritual. Required canonical ledger fields, unique grant IDs, active target/state and positive remaining amount are validated. Unknown sources and linked riders reject the scene. |
| One-shot healing reduction | Keep canonical effect ID and all past events. Consumption keys include the iteration. Snapshot-available Agony can be available in a new iteration before its original expiry; snapshot-consumed or expired Agony remains unavailable. |
| Soul Bind | Original absolute deadline, exact death instance for bound-dead records. An active pending record requires a living, non-Stable, dying zero-HP target with no death-instance binding. Application and target identities must match. Undoing a later death removes that later active bind. No revival event or source cost is manufactured. |
| Rewards | A claim belongs to encounter origin, immutable reward source, opportunity kind and source-defined slot. Another death event or iteration cannot make another claim. |
| Physical derivatives | Traverse immutable provenance transitively. A wholly in-scope, reversible temporal entity can retire; its costs stay spent. Surviving harvested inventory, mixed material roots, external source slots or persistent enrollment conflicts block the restore. Already consumed material remains consumed. |
| Outsiders | Keep body state, inventory ownership, resource history and concentration records. A snapshot dependency must still exist exactly and refer to the same live concentration ID. New current dependencies targeting restored participants need a supported overlay; otherwise they block. Unimplemented external anatomy/control/suppression overlays also block. |
| Environment | Each anchor has an exact canonical physical identity. Restore snapshot environment existence together with its geometry; remove both the physical derivative and its geometry when retiring a later temporal entity. Plan all participant positions simultaneously. Reject overlap, loss of support, and restrictions to a protected outsider's previously reachable ground area. This is deliberately limited to a finite orthogonal level ground plane, not flying, elevation, portals or mandatory growth. |
| Memory | The invoking Oracle and their immutable snapshot allies retain only facts individually perceived, experienced or received. Retained memories accumulate across loops. Enemy player characters receive no special knowledge; no hidden roster or Director facts enter memory automatically. |

## What the agreed rules mean at the table

These examples explain the reviewed boundaries. They do not enable the full ability before its remaining integrations are complete.

| Situation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| At initiative, an ally has25HP. Later they fall to3HP and spend8RP. Time Loop succeeds. | They return to25HP, limited by their current legal maximum. The8RP remain spent. Their snapshot encounter allowances return where the source explicitly permits it. |
| The same ally's legal maximum has fallen to20 because a conserved source changed. | They return to20HP. The reduction is temporal normalization, not damage or healing, and creates neither Wounds nor resource triggers. A structural progression change without its adapter instead makes the restore unavailable. |
| An ally began with a6-point Soul Cage shield, later lost it, and the original grant remains valid. | The same shield returns with its snapshot6 points. The Soul Charge paid for it remains spent. This is not a new cast, grant or recipient offer. |
| Oracle A uses Time Loop. Before A's next actual regular turn, Oracle B uses it too. | Both Oracles retain their Reaction debts. Rewinding does not clear A's debt. Each debt clears only at that Oracle's genuine normal Reaction refresh. |
| A restored enemy dies again after its reward opportunity was already claimed. | That same reward cannot be claimed again. The source opportunity, rather than the new death event, determines whether it was paid. |
| A body part was harvested after initiative and still exists as somebody else's item. | The generic restore is unavailable: it cannot duplicate the body part or take away the current owner's item. A specifically reviewed reconciliation would be required. |
| An ally saw a hidden passage in the discarded timeline; another ally never learned about it. | The witness can retain that memory if eligible through the invoking Oracle's snapshot alliance. The other ally receives no automatic knowledge. The witness can tell them normally. |

An unavailable restore spends neither the Reaction nor the long-rest entitlement. The Director needs a complete, legal proposed state before resolving the ability; unresolved source interactions cannot be waived by calling a snapshot complete.
